finding: NIO absorbed a RMB 10,000/vehicle purchase-tax subsidy on ES8 orders locked through 30 April 2026 and then discontinued it mid-Q2 — Deutsche Bank named that discontinuation as a cause of the June ES8 order shortfall. ES8 (Gen 3) was 33,474 units of Q2's 107,658, so removing RMB 10,000/unit from even ~18,000 Q2 deliveries retains ~RMB 180m of margin, which is the whole of Deutsche Bank's ~RMB 180m Q2 non-GAAP net income estimate. The 2.1% unit miss versus the 110-115k guide was in part the price paid for that margin, not purely demand weakness.
why_not_priced: The delivery miss is a published monthly number every terminal has; the subsidy withdrawal that partly caused it is a line item disclosed only in Chinese-language promo terms and a CnEVPost analyst note, and it works in the opposite direction on the P&L. If the market had joined the two, the stock would not be sitting at its 52-week low on a 'profitability doubt' narrative into a quarter where the per-unit subsidy drag was actively being removed — you would see previews framing the unit miss as margin-accretive, and there are none.
independence: Overlaps with finding 2 (both are opex/margin mechanisms behind the profitability run) but is a separate line of the P&L. Corroborated independently by the 2026-04-02 CnEVPost piece documenting the RMB 10,000 ES8 purchase-tax subsidy and its 30 April cutoff: https://cnevpost.com/2026/04/02/nio-es8-deliveries-16255-mar-2026/

NIO never gave aggregate numbers during 2025, calling it 'organizational optimization'. Q2 2026 volume was +29% sequentially (107,658 vs 83,465) against that reduced cost base.

If this were priced you would see it in the preview arithmetic as an explicit opex step-down, and consensus would not still be modelling a full-year loss of CN¥1.69/share. independence: Partially overlaps finding 1 (both explain the profitability turn). Independent secondary extraction of the same table: https://eletric-vehicles.com/nio/nio-discloses-10600-job-cuts-in-2025-with-40-of-rd-staff-eliminated/

finding: NIO's year-on-year growth rate collapses mechanically from the August number onward on base effects, and 1 September is NIO's established monthly-delivery publication slot, so the August figure plausibly lands in the same tape as Q2 results and the Q3 guide. Bottom-up August 2026 indicators point to roughly flat-to-modestly-up sequentially (third-gen ES8's latest 10,000 units took 30 days as of 21 August; Onvo L60 at 3,201 units in the first 28 days), implying Q3 near 113-118k and YoY growth roughly halving to ~+30%.
why_not_priced: The sell-side has these comps; the marginal holder of a $4.37 ADS does not, and the narrative in circulation is the '+71% year-on-year' July headline. The structural half of this is the sharper point: NIO filed monthly delivery 6-Ks on 2026-06-01, 2026-07-02 and 2026-08-03 for the prior month, so 1 September is the slot for August, and no aggregator flags that this print carries three releases at once. If the market had this, the front-expiry implied move would sit above the 9.76% single-event level to reflect a compound catalyst, and the put/call open interest ratio would not be 0.32.
independence: Independent of findings 1, 2 and 4. Corroborated by the July 2026 delivery release (35,934, +71.0%): https://cnevpost.com/2026/08/01/nio-deliveries-jul-2026/ and the 6-K filing-date cadence on EDGAR.

finding: The syndicated Q1 FY27 consensus revenue of $9.47bn (+10.4% on the $8,578m year-ago base) sits roughly a point below what Medtronic's own 3 June quarterly guidance implies — 11.5% to 12.0% organic growth plus a 'neutral to $50 million' FX tailwind plus acquired revenue from CathWorks/Scientia/SPR, i.e. about $9.55-9.65bn — while consensus EPS of $1.39 is exactly the midpoint of the guided $1.38-$1.40; the same one-point gap exists at the full-year level ($38.85bn consensus vs 6.75-7.25% organic on $36,364m plus 0-1% FX plus M&A). The likeliest cause is incomplete modelling of the 53rd selling week, which management sized at 500-600bps of Q1 revenue but 600-700bps of Q1 EPS, so the EPS line was captured and part of the revenue line was not. Mechanically this makes a print that merely lands on guidance read in the wire copy as a $100-180m top-line beat.
why_not_priced: Nobody publishes the reconciliation of a consensus print against the company's own quarterly guide, and the inconsistency is visible only as an internal contradiction in the estimate set (EPS on guidance, revenue below it). If it were priced, previews would be flagging a 'low bar on revenue' rather than quoting the $9.47bn as the bar; instead Zacks' preview quotes it straight. I keep the size small and let the band cross zero because the marginal holder of a mega-cap trades the buy-side bar, not the Zacks bar, and MDT has twice in the last four prints sold off on a headline beat.
independence: Overlaps only in direction with the Needham note (PT $101 to $114, expects a beat and a guidance raise, https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/needham-raises-medtronic-stock-price-target-on-product-cycle-93CH-4879312); the arithmetic itself is independent of any broker note and rests on the transcript plus the $8,578m base in the 2025-08-19 release.

On 3 June management said separation was expected 'prior to year-end' and explicitly framed early separation as potential upside to FY27 guidance, which assumes twelve months of Diabetes consolidation. Compounding it, MMED traded at $18.92 on 2026-08-26, below its $20.00 March IPO price, which weakens the discount economics of a split-off and raises the odds of a plain pro-rata spin-off that would retire none of Medtronic's ~1.28bn shares.

If the market had priced a slip, previews would be discussing whether FY27 guidance gets re-based rather than repeating the June 'full twelve months of Diabetes' framing. The band crosses zero because the standard sequencing is to launch an exchange offer immediately after a quarterly release, so the same fact can flip to a positive on 1 September.
independence: Cross-checked against Medtronic's own EDGAR index (no 8-K since 2026-06-03, https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001613103&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=60) and against the 2026-08-17 DEF 14A, whose only capital resolution is the routine annual 'overseas market purchases' authority, with no off-market purchase or exchange-offer resolution for the 15 October AGM.

Both of the up-prints in the baseline's eight-event history were beat-and-raise / M&A-news events (2025-06-03 +31.5%, 2025-08-18 +8.8%) - a guidance raise is now impossible and there is no Q&A in which management can reframe a weak metric.
why_not_priced: Aggregators still model YEXT as a normal call-and-guide company - MarketBeat-derived previews for 1 Sep still reference a conference call, and the calendar row that generated this event carries the AMC-style convention that seven of the last eight prints used. The practical consequence is a truncated upside tail: everything lands in one 8-K pre-open with no management voice, so the reaction is a pure read of the metrics table. finding: A company that says it gives no guidance did quietly set a hard numerical bar for this exact quarter, buried in the 2 Jun shareholder letter: 'GAAP Net Income margins in the 10-15% range in Q2, Q3 and Q4' and 'Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion towards 30%'. Q1 FY27 GAAP net income was only ~2.2% of revenue ($0.02 basic EPS on $107.9m), so hitting the low end of its own range in Q2 requires GAAP net income of roughly $11-17m - a 4-7x sequential jump - against a rising interest bill on $150m of newly drawn term debt.
why_not_priced: No aggregator carries it, because the company is formally 'no guidance' so the screens have nothing to populate: the $0.17 consensus is a non-GAAP diluted number (Zacks used the same basis for Q1: $0.13 est vs $0.14 actual) and therefore does not measure the GAAP-margin promise at all. A stock that had priced this would show a visible GAAP net income estimate line, and there is none. Two-sided: the non-GAAP $0.17 bar looks beatable on the post-tender share count alone, so the likely shape is 'EPS beat, self-set GAAP margin bar missed' - the same split that produced -9% on 2 Jun.
independence: Debt and Q1 GAAP figures from the 10-Q: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1614178/000162828026039788/yext-20260430.htm ($150.0m term loan principal, $91.9m cash + $29.2m securities, $0.4m tax provision, $4.3m HQ sublease impairment). Independent of findings 1-4.

finding: The demand that is accelerating is SPWH's lowest-margin demand: Q1 2026 gross margin fell to 29.6% from 30.4% specifically because firearms and ammunition mix rose while higher-margin categories declined, Q1 adjusted EBITDA was -$8.1m against a full-year guide of $30-36m that is therefore entirely back-half-loaded, and Academy told investors on 10 June 2026 -- eight days after SPWH last spoke -- that it was 'tracking at flat comparable sales through the Memorial Day period' on 'persistent $4+ gas prices'.

If the market had worked this through, the coverage would frame a firearms-led beat as margin-dilutive rather than as good news, and the 30 Aug preview would not simply say 'revenue flat'. Academy's flat-through-Memorial-Day comment is the reason I do not extrapolate the whole +7.7% NICS quarter into comps -- the non-firearm half of the box (camp, apparel, footwear) is still fighting $4 gasoline.

OVERLAP DISCLOSED: this finding and finding 1 read the SAME underlying fact -- firearms/ammunition-led growth -- on opposite lines of the P&L (revenue vs gross margin rate). It is filed as a signed offset, not as independent negative evidence, and finding 1's +5.0 is already net of a gross-margin haircut; the two together are one thesis with an honest downside vent, not two theses. finding: The baseline's 20-day average volume of 405,662 shares is essentially one session: GMHS traded 7,142,358 shares on 2026-08-31 (+16.51%) with no company filing or press release on or around that date, while the surrounding sessions traded 6,192 (2026-08-13), 19,279 (2026-08-11), 22,908 (2026-08-12), 35,144 (2026-08-27) and 66,901 (2026-08-28) shares - so the true book into this print is tens of thousands of shares a day, and the +16.5% spike has already bled off across four consecutive down days to $0.77.

With no options market there is no implied move to correct it, and the 20-day ADV that would normally warn a reader about liquidity has been inflated ~8x by a single unexplained session. If the market were pricing this correctly the name would carry a visible illiquidity discount and a much wider historic reaction distribution than the 4.19% median the baseline reports; instead one 17x-volume day is being read as normal turnover. Practically: a print-day order of ordinary institutional size cannot be filled without moving GMHS by a large multiple of 4.19% in whichever direction it arrives.
independence: none

finding: US energy storage installed a record 20.2 GWh in calendar Q2 2026 (17.9-18.0 GWh utility-scale, 1.8 GWh commercial/industrial), 30.8 GWh in H1, and SEIA/Benchmark RAISED the full-year 2026 forecast to 71 GWh versus 59 GWh installed in 2025 - published 2026-09-01, twelve weeks after ABM last spoke, and covering the two months (May, June) that sit inside ABM's fiscal Q3.
why_not_priced: ABM's Technical Solutions grew 27.2% in Q2 FY26 explicitly on battery energy storage, and the entire FY26 adjusted-EPS guide rests on management's claim that 'volume will ramp meaningfully in ATS' in the back half - the single most doubted line in the guide, because ATS margin was diluted in Q2 by equipment-heavy BESS work. Directionally corroborated by a separate, unrelated demand channel - hyperscaler capex guidance was raised again at the late-July/early-August 2026 prints (Amazon to ~$220bn from ~$200bn, Alphabet to $195-205bn from $180-190bn) per https://www.tmtfinance.com/intel/2026-hyperscaler-capex-tops-us700bn-analysis - which feeds the same ATS data-centre electrical book. Shares no document with any other finding in this file.

finding: CBRE's Q2 2026 US office report (2026-07-29) shows national vacancy falling 30bp to 18.3% - 'the largest quarterly decline since 2015' - net absorption of 12.6m sq ft, nearly double the prior quarter and a ninth straight positive quarter, leasing +16% y/y, with CBRE projecting 2026 annual leasing to surpass the 2022 record; San Francisco, the exact market ABM's CEO singled out on 2026-06-05 as having vacancy 'probably 2 or 3x worse than New York City', posted +963,980 sq ft of net absorption in the quarter.
why_not_priced: Business & Industry is ~44% of ABM revenue ($1,015.8m of $2,290.0m in Q2) and was flat y/y, which management attributed to UK and West Coast client exits driven by CRE weakness. The office inflection is fully priced in office REITs, which are the constituency that reads CBRE Figures; it is not priced in a janitorial contractor covered by three analysts, because the transmission runs through re-scoping, occupancy-linked hours and win rates rather than through any line an ABM preview models. If it were priced you would see ABM bid into the print rather than -3.07% over 20 days, and you would see at least one of the three estimates moving after 2026-07-29. Sized small deliberately: janitorial scope lags leasing by several quarters, and near-term reported B&I is dominated by the disclosed Transport for London exit worth ~300bp of back-half B&I growth, so this is a tone-and-FY27 item more than a Q3 revenue item.
independence: A different firm, different methodology, same direction and published separately: Colliers' Q2 2026 US office statistics report the strongest quarterly net absorption in seven years with national vacancy at ~18% - https://www.colliers.com/en/research/nrep-usofc-us-office-market-statistics-2026-q2. San Francisco detail is a second CBRE document (https://www.cbre.com/insights/figures/san-francisco-office-figures-q2-2026, 2026-07-10), so treat the two CBRE files as one source cluster with Colliers as the genuinely independent leg.

finding: ABM Aviation grew 19.5% in Q2 and its CEO warned on 2026-06-05 that 'rising fuel costs will likely create some near-term challenges for our airline clients'; since then the airline cost shock deepened rather than resolved - American Airlines cut FY26 guidance a second time in July (to a -$0.65 to +$0.65 adjusted EPS range from -$0.40 to +$1.10, with a Q3 loss guide, on ~$3.75/gal fuel), Southwest cut FY26 to $3.25-$4.25 from 'at least $4' after a ~$900m y/y Q2 fuel increase, and Alaska has had guidance suspended since April.
why_not_priced: Aviation is 13.5% of ABM revenue ($310.8m, $16.3m segment operating profit in Q2) and was the second-fastest-growing segment, and the market is extrapolating the Heathrow ramp. Airline distress is completely priced in airline equities - it is not priced in a name screened as defensive facility services, and none of the three published ABM estimates models an airline procurement squeeze on outsourced cabin, ground and passenger-assistance scope. If the market had priced it, ABM's 25-delta skew would be visibly bid for downside and the stock would be more than 4.68% off its high with realised vol above 15%. Sized small on purpose and honestly: TSA throughput set records through June and July 2026 so in-quarter volumes were fine, the direct Q3 EPS arithmetic of even a 5% Aviation revenue shortfall is roughly a penny, most ABM airline contracts pass through labour, and the industry capacity trim was already partly visible before ABM guided on 2026-06-05. The risk here is to forward commentary and FY27 framing, not to the Q3 number.
independence: Partial only. BofA's carrier-capacity tracking (Q3 2026 domestic growth cut to ~0.8%, American to 7.5% from 9.3%, Delta to 1.2%) points the same way - https://m.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/bofa-cuts-airline-capacity-outlook-as-carriers-trim-september-plans-93CH-4710071 - but that page carries a corrupt primary timestamp and a 2026-05-26 update stamp, i.e. it may pre-date ABM's guide, so I am not resting the finding on it. The ABM-side leg is management's own 2026-06-05 remark in the transcript: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/08/abm-abm-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/

finding: Note 8 of the Q2 FY26 10-Q states that ABM performed its review of the majority of its casualty insurance programmes during Q2 2026 and 'it was determined that there was no adjustment required for our total reserves related to prior years during the six months ended April 30, 2026' - so the item that produced a $(22.2)m pre-tax hit (~100bp of adjusted EBITDA margin, ~$0.26/sh) in Q4 FY25 is a Q2/Q4 event and is very unlikely to appear in the Q3 print, even though ABM's adjusted EPS definition now includes it while its guidance range is stated 'before any impact from prior-year self-insurance adjustments'.
why_not_priced: ABM changed its non-GAAP definition after SEC staff comment (disclosed 2025-12-17) so that reported adjusted EPS now INCLUDES prior-year self-insurance adjustments, while the $3.85-$4.15 guide explicitly excludes them. That mismatch is the mechanical reason FY25 landed at $3.44 against a $3.65-$3.80 range, and it is the most plausible single source of a headline 'miss' on this name. Three analysts on a $2.8bn company are not reading Note 8 of a June 10-Q to work out the actuarial cadence, and there is no aggregator field for 'timing of casualty reserve reviews'. If the market had priced the absence of this risk you would not see an indicative 8.13% implied move on a 93-contract chain with a 1.32 put/call OI ratio. This is a left-tail-removal finding, not a mean finding, which is why it is sized at less than half a point.
independence: The $(22.2)m Q4 FY25 magnitude and the non-GAAP definition change come from a different document - the FY25 results release, https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/12/17/3206839/799/en/ABM-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-2025-Results-and-Provides-Fiscal-2026-Outlook.html (2025-12-17). No other finding in this file rests on the 10-Q, so there is no source-cluster overlap.

finding: Waterdrop's entire revenue growth story is one line: technical service income went RMB1.8m (Q4 2024) to RMB9.4m (Q1 2025) to RMB639.6m (Q4 2025) to RMB421.0m (Q1 2026) -- so it already fell 34.2% sequentially in Q1 2026 -- while brokerage income, the actual insurance business, was RMB648.6m / RMB670.8m / RMB724.8m over the same span, i.e. +11.7% YoY against the +64.8% headline, with sales and marketing rising from 22.9% to 43.6% of revenue and net profit falling to RMB98.4m from RMB108.2m.

If the market had done the arithmetic, the last print on 2026-06-17 would not have paid +2.34% for a quarter in which net profit fell 9.1% YoY and the sole growth engine turned down 34% QoQ; there would be a published EPS consensus (there is none), and the only sell-side note on the tape would not be a UOB Kay Hian buy at US$2.20 dated 2025-03-14 (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/WDH/waterdrop-inc-receives-a-buy-rating-from-uob-kay-hian-with-price-lcl1sqnsy0x3.html), eighteen months stale and citing FY2024 net profit growth of 119.8%. independence: Two separate Chinese outlets reached the same conclusion from the same disclosure without the QoQ inflection: Sina Finance, 2026-03-27, flagged the 354x jump to RMB639.6m and that it is 48.82% of insurance-related income with the composition and buyers undisclosed (https://finance.sina.com.cn/roll/2026-03-27/doc-inhsmnzp9505963.shtml), and Tencent News, 2026-04-11, argued the company 'spends more than one yuan to generate one yuan in revenue growth' (https://news.qq.com/rain/a/20260411A07DEQ00). The Q4 2025 RMB639.6m and the S&M/operating-profit series are cross-checked against the company's own Q4 exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1823986/000110465926034227/tm269697d1_ex99-1.htm) and the Q2 2025 release, whose RMB97.3m operating profit matches my FY-minus-quarters derivation exactly. finding: Huize Holding, the closest listed Chinese online life/health insurance brokerage, reported H1 2026 on 2026-08-20 with gross written premium +29.8% and first-year premium +48.7% but operating revenue up only 5.8% -- revenue per unit of premium fell from 21.1% to 17.2%, an 18.5% relative collapse in the channel take rate, in exactly the April-June window Waterdrop is about to report.

finding: The US$50 million share repurchase authorisation expires on 2026-09-09 -- the day after this print -- with the great majority unused (cumulative buybacks moved only from US$118.1m to US$120.1m between the Q4 and Q1 releases, and the 20-F puts usage under the September 2025 programme at US$9.5m as of 2026-03-31), and Waterdrop has launched a new programme in September 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 and declared a US$0.03/ADS cash dividend alongside both its Q2 2025 and Q4 2025 results.

A fresh authorisation of up to US$50m is roughly 11-14% of the US$366m market cap and about 190 sessions of the 254,685-ADS average volume, on a stock whose US$417.6m cash position exceeds its market cap. The low end of my range is negative because the board has a live reason to skip the dividend this time: US$0.03 is 2.9% of a $1.02 spot and the ex-date would mechanically push the price under $1.00, so a dividend the holder base has come to expect could instead be cut or deferred.
independence: The five-programme history is stated in a different company document, the Q3 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1823986/000110465925117939/tm2532559d2_ex99-1.htm, 2025-12-03): 'Pursuant to the share repurchase programs launched in September 2021, September 2022, September 2023, September 2024, and September 2025'. finding: WDH's NYSE Rule 802.01C 30-trading-day average closing price is $1.0263 as of 2026-09-04 (window 2026-07-27 to 2026-09-04), and the five sessions rolling out of that window closed $1.15/$1.15/$1.15/$1.14/$1.12, so the next five closes must average at least $0.984 to keep the average above $1.00 -- roughly 3.5% of cushion from the $1.02 spot, with the print the only scheduled catalyst inside that window.
why_not_priced: This is a computation, not a disclosure: it requires taking 30 daily closes and averaging them, and no company release, no aggregator field and no wire story states it. The eye-catching detail in the same series is that WDH closed at exactly $1.00 for thirteen consecutive sessions (2026-08-05 to 2026-08-21) and exactly $0.99 for the six after -- a pin, not a random walk, on a $260k/day notional. If the threshold were priced, the run-in would show either accelerating decline or a squeeze, not nineteen sessions of a flat line inside a one-cent band; and there would be an English-language story on it, of which there are none. Signed slightly negative because a $1.02 stock five sessions from a non-compliance notice has a fatter left tail on a bad print -- mandates that cannot hold non-compliant names sell -- while the offsetting 'management acts to support the price' channel is already carried in the buyback finding above.
independence: Two Chinese outlets flag the threshold without doing the arithmetic: China Financial Online, 2026-08-06, 'Waterdrop's share price touches the warning line' (http://sc.stock.cnfol.com/gushijujiao/20260806/32327351.shtml), and a China Business Herald report of 2026-07-25 cited there on overseas-listed insurtechs falling below the US$1 line. Shares direction with, but is arithmetically independent of, the buyback finding; the price series is a different source from any company filing.

finding: The EU 21st-package carve-out that drove DLNG from $3.32 (16 July) to $3.85 (23 July) is a third-country-deliveries-only derogation expiring 25 July 2027, renewable one year at a time by Council vote and capped at the operator's 2025 volumes; the AIS work identifying the Dynagas vessels it protects names Clean Planet, Clean Vision, Clean Ocean and Clean Horizon - none of which are among the listed partnership's six ships - while DLNG's own Yamal-chartered Lena River last called at Huelva, Spain, an EU import terminal, departing 25 August 2026, i.e. exactly the EU-delivery employment the derogation does not cover.
why_not_priced: Dynagas holds no earnings call and has said nothing in writing since 29 May 2026, when its 6-K still stated that losing the Yamal charters 'would have a material adverse effect' and that it was studying 'the feasibility of lawfully removing the E.U. nexus'; the 8 September release is the first company text after the derogation. If the market had read the derogation's terms rather than the headline it would not have paid +9.17% and +4.34% on 22-23 July and then held most of it - and a $135m MLP with no analyst coverage, no EPS estimate and 41 contracts of total option open interest has no mechanism through which anyone reconciled the Official Journal text with which four hulls actually sit inside the listed entity. Coverage, if this were priced, would look like a note distinguishing the sponsor's Arc7 fleet from the MLP's 1A fleet; no such note exists.
independence: Two separate documents reach the same reading of the text independently of the urgewald analysis: euobserver, 27 July 2026, states the exemption covers LNG 'to third countries' and explicitly not European deliveries (https://euobserver.com/230246/brussels-found-russias-lng-weak-spot-then-carved-out-an-exception-for-a-greek-billionaire/), and High North News, 4 August 2026, gives the 25 July 2027 expiry, the annual Council renewal and the 2025 volume cap (https://en.highnorthnews.com/politics/eu-softens-russian-lng-sanctions-allowing-shipping-and-trading-to-continue-beyond-2027/1115356). The fleet-identity leg is independently checkable against the partnership's own Q1 6-K, which lists its six vessels as Clean Energy, Ob River, Amur River, Arctic Aurora, Yenisei River and Lena River (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1578453/000131786126000029/f052926dlng6k.htm). NOTE ON CLUSTERING: the vessel-identity leg and the destination-split leg both come out of the same urgewald document, so treat them as one source, not two.

finding: Clean Energy, the vessel DLNG moved onto a Rio Grande LNG charter 'at higher daily rates' at the end of April 2026, has sat at anchor in Southeast Asia in ballast (draught 8.9 m, speed 0.1 knots) with no destination and no ETA since departing Singapore Anchorage on 5 August 2026 - 33 days idle - while Arctic Aurora, still trading normally (loaded at Melkoya, Norway on 7 September for Klaipeda), is contracted to begin a second seven-year Rio Grande charter between September and November 2026, which would put a third of the six-ship fleet on hire to a project company whose Brownsville trains are not yet producing.
why_not_priced: Nobody aggregates AIS for a 50k-ADV MLP. This does not touch Q2 revenue - Q2 ended 30 June and time-charter hire is paid whether the ship moves or not - so the channel is the presentation's fleet-employment page and any disclosure of sublet or restructured arrangements with Rio Grande LNG, LLC, plus the Arctic Aurora delivery window. Had the market focused on it, a name whose entire equity story is charter counterparty quality would carry commentary on a pre-operational charterer holding two of six hulls; there is none, and the July rally treated the charter book as de-risked rather than concentrated. I am deliberately sizing this small because the contractual cash flow is unaffected.
independence: Two other vessels checked the same day on separate pages show the idling is not fleet-wide, which is what makes the Clean Energy datum interpretable rather than a data artefact: Ob River is en route Anjeong, Korea (departed 5 September) to Zhuhai, China (https://www.vesselfinder.com/vessels/details/9315692), and Arctic Aurora departed Melkoya, Norway on 7 September at 18.3 knots for Klaipeda (https://www.vesselfinder.com/vessels/details/9645970). Separately, the partnership's Q1 6-K is the source for the end-April Rio Grande delivery and the 'higher daily rates' characterisation (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1578453/000131786126000029/f052926dlng6k.htm).

finding: Six directors of Dynagas LNG Partners filed initial Section 16 ownership statements on 18 and 30 March 2026, every one of them carrying event date 18 March 2026 - George Prokopiou reporting 15,595,000 common units and 35,526 GP units indirectly through Dynagas Holding Ltd (50.4% beneficial interest), Alexios Rodopoulos 500 units direct, Dimitrios Anagnostopoulos 'no securities owned' - even though the partnership is exempt from Section 16 as a foreign private issuer under Rule 3a12-3(b), filed a 20-F for FY2025 on 8 April 2026 and has continued filing 6-Ks rather than 10-Qs through 13 August 2026; no Form 4 has followed in the five and a half months since.
why_not_priced: I am filing this at zero because I could not resolve it, not because it is unimportant: it is a genuine contradiction in the filing record that I can document and cannot explain. A board that becomes Section 16 reporting normally means the issuer has concluded it no longer qualifies as a foreign private issuer, which would force 10-Q/10-K/8-K, US-GAAP-only reporting and proxy statements - or it is the compliance footprint of a transaction. Neither has surfaced. If the market had noticed, a $135m MLP would show speculation about domestic-filer conversion or a going-private, and the 8 September event would not be scheduled as a 6-K with no conference call. I refuse to guess a sign, so it carries no directional weight; the band is width, not a view.
independence: none - the only corroboration is that the same EDGAR submissions index shows both the Form 3 cluster and the continuing 6-K/20-F pattern, which is the same source (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001578453.json), and no press, filing or company statement anywhere explains the 18 March 2026 event date.

finding: UNFI's own narrowed FY26 guide implies Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $156-176mm, but the company itself quantified the prior-year Q4 as depressed by $40-50mm of cyber-incident adjusted EBITDA, so on a cyber-clean basis Q4 FY26 EBITDA is roughly flat to +13% (mid ~+3%) against reported growth of +34% to +52%, and against +23.4% in Q2 and +16.6% in Q3 — the underlying run-rate that has to support a ~$745-760mm FY27 guide on the way to the $800mm FY28 Investor Day target has decelerated to near zero.
why_not_priced: The arithmetic requires stitching three documents together: 39-week actuals (26-week adj EBITDA $346mm from the 2026-03-10 8-K plus $183mm Q3 from the 2026-06-09 8-K = $529mm), the narrowed FY26 guide of $685-705mm, and the July 2025 8-K's $40-50mm cyber EBITDA quantification. If the market had done it, the published Q4 consensus would not be sitting exactly on the guide midpoint (rev $7.705bn vs guide-implied $7.590-7.790bn; EPS $0.612 vs guide-implied $0.45-0.65, i.e. the 81st percentile of the company's own range) — consensus is modelling the reported optic, not the clean run-rate, and there is no visible FY27 whisper on a name the aggregators show with 2 estimates.
independence: Same-document cluster warning: the 39-week actuals and the guide come from UNFI's Q2/Q3 8-Ks, and the cyber quantification from the July 2025 8-K, so this is one arithmetic chain, not three findings. It shares its conclusion (FY27 guide risk) with the new-CFO finding below and the two should be read as overlapping. Independent corroboration of the FY28 anchor it is measured against: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1020859/000102085925000070/a2025investordaypressrelea.htm (Investor Day, 2025-12-10, ~$33bn sales / ~$800mm adjusted EBITDA / ~$300mm FCF by FY28).

finding: SNAP enrollment fell from 42.2 million in May 2025 to 36.6 million in May 2026 (-13%, faster than CBO projected, with Arizona -55%, Florida -22%), and this data was published on 2026-08-21 — after UNFI last guided on 2026-06-09; UNFI's Conventional ($3.136bn) plus Retail ($515mm) segments were ~47% of Q3 FY26 net sales and are precisely the SNAP-exposed channels.
why_not_priced: UNFI is modelled as a natural/organic growth story, not a SNAP name — its Q3 narrative and the sell-side framing are Natural segment growth and network optimisation, and management has never quantified SNAP exposure on a call. If this were priced into UNFI specifically you would see Conventional-segment estimates cut and the FY27 sales bridge debated; instead UNFI reiterated its FY26 midpoints on 2026-06-09 and the coverage that followed argued about the revenue miss, not the channel. The SNAP theme is priced into Kroger/Dollar General; it is not priced into the wholesaler two steps upstream.
independence: Circana estimates total SNAP EBT will fall ~$10bn in 2026 versus 2025, a separate commercial estimate from a separate publisher: https://www.foodmanufacturing.com/consumer-trends/news/22972889/enrollment-in-snap-grocery-aid-is-dropping-faster-than-expected (2026-08-21).

finding: Both listed natural-channel retailers reported negative traffic inside UNFI's Q4 window (2026-05-03 to 2026-08-01): Natural Grocers' quarter ended 2026-06-30 showed daily-average comps +1.2% built entirely on a +3.1% basket with transaction count -1.8% and gross margin down 60bp, and Sprouts' June quarter showed comps -1% with management citing weaker June trends — while UNFI's Natural segment (+4.4% in Q3) is the only growing part of the company and the pillar of the FY27 return-to-growth guide.
why_not_priced: Nobody carries UNFI and NGVC in the same model — NGVC is a $335mm-a-quarter retailer and UNFI is a $31bn wholesaler, and the read-through runs the wrong way for a screener. If the market had made this link, the negative-unit-volume debate would be in the UNFI previews (which instead lead on the easy cyber comp and the +$0.62-vs-$(0.11) EPS optic) and UNFI's Natural-segment growth estimate would have been cut after 2026-08-06. NGVC itself fell 14% on the print, so the channel datapoint moved a price — just not this one.
independence: Sprouts Farmers Market's June-quarter comp of -1% with explicit weaker-June commentary is a second, larger, independently sourced natural-channel datapoint: https://www.grocerydive.com/news/sprouts-farmers-market-second-quarter-results-self-distribution-new-store-openings-loyalty/826603/ . Cuts the other way, and I am counting it: Amazon's physical-stores line held +4% over the same window (see next finding).

finding: Amazon's physical-stores net sales — the reported line for Whole Foods, UNFI's largest customer at roughly a quarter of net sales — were $5,794mm in the June-2026 quarter versus $5,595mm a year earlier, +4% and +4% excluding FX, essentially unchanged from the +4.6% March-quarter pace, covering two-thirds of UNFI's Q4.
why_not_priced: Customer concentration is the standing bear case on UNFI and the reason the put skew sits at +6.97 points, but the one hard, contemporaneous, third-party measurement of that customer's volume during the quarter being reported sits in an Amazon 8-K exhibit that no UNFI preview cites. If it were priced, the previews would say Whole Foods sell-through was steady through July rather than treating the Whole Foods exposure as an unmeasured risk; instead the risk is discussed only through the 2032 contract term. It also removes one of the two live explanations for a Q4 revenue miss, leaving only the deliberate Allentown/Sturtevant optimisation.
independence: The contract term itself is independently confirmed to May 2032, so this is volume news rather than renewal news: https://ir.unfi.com/news/press-release-details/2024/United-Natural-Foods-Inc.-Extends-Distribution-Partnership-with-Whole-Foods-Market-to-2032/default.aspx . Nothing else I found measures Whole Foods volume directly.

finding: UNFI pulled its Q4/full-year report forward roughly three weeks against a stable four-year pattern — 2026-09-08 versus 2025-09-30, 2024-10-01 and late September in the two prior years — and announced the new date on 2026-08-10, the exact day the incoming CFO started, five and a half weeks after a 1 August fiscal year end.
why_not_priced: Calendar aggregators carry the date, not the change in the date — the row reads 2026-09-08 with no memory that this company has reported Q4 in the last week of September or the first day of October every year since FY2022, so the timing shift leaves no trace in coverage or in the option chain. A company finalising a full-year audit and a fresh long-range plan five and a half weeks after year end, with a CFO four weeks into the job, is not behaving like one that needs time. I am scoring this small because I could not rule out the benign explanation: Barclays' Global Consumer Staples Conference runs 2026-09-09, the day after, and staples issuers routinely report just ahead of it — I could not confirm UNFI on that agenda either way.
independence: Prior-year date confirmed in a separate, independently dated release: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20240911386565/en/United-Natural-Foods-to-Release-Fiscal-2024-Fourth-Quarter-Results-on-October-1-2024 (2024-09-11).

finding: The initial FY27 guide — the single largest swing factor in this print — will be delivered by a CFO who started on 2026-08-10, four weeks before, as part of four senior changes in seven weeks around the fiscal year end: Matteo Tarditi moved off CFO to President/COO, Alfredo Luchini arrived as CFO from Carrier, supply-chain head Mark Bushway was announced as departing 2027-01-01, and Chief Corporate Affairs Officer Matthew Echols ceased in the role on 2026-08-24.
why_not_priced: The personnel facts are in an 8-K, but the consequence for this specific print is not in any preview: UNFI's two 20%-class up-moves (2024-12-10 +20.02%, 2025-09-30 +18.45%) were both guide-setting prints delivered by Tarditi, who set FY26 deliberately low ($1.50-2.30 adjusted EPS) and raised the midpoint to $2.50 over three quarters. A first-print CFO inheriting a public $800mm FY28 target he did not set has an asymmetric incentive to anchor FY27 at the bottom of that path. If the market had focused on this, the 12.5% implied would be skewed toward a guidance-reset outcome rather than symmetric around a spot 21% off the high, and previews would be discussing who owns the FY27 number.
independence: The Echols exit is a separate document (Form 4 with no transactions, 2026-08-27): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001020859/000162828026059263/wk-form4_1787862228.xml . This finding overlaps with the Q4-EBITDA-arithmetic finding above — both resolve into FY27 guide risk — and the two should be collapsed to roughly one and a half findings, not two.

finding: UNFI's fuel hedge book is a $5m Level-2 current asset as of 2026-05-02 (up from $1m at 2026-01-31) - trivially small against a $1.87/gal year-over-year diesel move - and being entirely current it expires inside FY27, exactly the year whose guide is set on 8 September, with US on-highway diesel at $5.599/gal on 2026-08-31 (+$1.865 YoY) after having fallen to $4.578 on 2026-07-06.
why_not_priced: On the 9 June call management named 'fuel hedging' first of three mitigation levers when pressed on fuel by R5 Capital, and that framing is what the market is working from; the 10-Q fair-value table shows the hedge is a $5m current asset, i.e. immaterial and expiring, and the DERIVATIVES note itself lists only interest-rate swaps so a reader of the note alone would never see the fuel book at all. If the market had read this, a preview would describe the hedge as de minimis rather than as a mitigant, and the two-estimate FY27 consensus would carry an explicit fuel line. The separate and larger point the price cannot yet hold is the path: diesel fell to $4.578 in early July, making the fuel scare look resolved, then re-spiked to a record, so the fuel curve against which the FY27 guide must be set is materially worse than the one visible when management last spoke. I am discounting heavily because the -4.08% five-day run-in overlaps the week diesel set its record, which is evidence the market is pricing some of this.
independence: Two independent non-SEC sources point the same way: the EIA weekly retail diesel series (https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=pet&s=emd_epd2d_pte_nus_dpg&f=W, showing $3.897 on 2026-03-02 rising to $5.401, $5.640 through May, $4.578 on 2026-07-06 and $5.652 on 2026-08-24) and Fortune's 2026-09-04 report of a record $5.85/gal explicitly tied to grocery supply chains (https://fortune.com/2026/09/04/diesel-record-price-groceries/). Note the 'higher freight costs' line in finding 2 corroborates this same cost thesis - treat the two as partially overlapping, not additive.

finding: Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage, which buys 69% of its product from UNFI, reported its quarter ended 2026-06-30 - sitting entirely inside UNFI's Q4 - with net sales up only 1.8%, daily average transaction COUNT down 1.8%, gross margin down 60bp on unfavourable mix and higher freight, and cut the top end of both its FY26 EPS guide ($2.15 to $2.11) and its comp guide (2.5% to 2.0%), all against a prior-year base that its own release says was distorted by the cybersecurity incident at its primary distributor.
why_not_priced: NGVC's release never names UNFI, and nothing bridges a small natural-foods retailer's 8-K to a $2.7bn wholesaler's Q4 - UNFI carries two published estimates, so there is no mechanism by which such a read-through gets marked. If it were priced you would see UNFI's natural-segment growth expectation publicly stepped down from the +4.4% posted in Q3, and there is no revision note doing that. The specific unpriced content is the direction of units: NGVC grew dollars 1.8% while shrinking traffic 1.8% against a comp depressed by UNFI's own June-2025 outage, which implies natural-channel case volume in UNFI's Q4 was weaker than the Q3 exit rate rather than stronger.
independence: Amazon's Q2 2026 supplemental shows Physical Stores (predominantly Whole Foods, UNFI's largest customer) at $5,794m vs $5,595m, +4% - steady rather than accelerating, so it neither confirms nor contradicts, and it is the reason my band crosses zero: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872426000024/amzn-20260630xex991.htm. The freight-cost element of this finding shares a cost driver with finding 1 and should not be counted twice.

finding: Five senior officer changes between 2026-07-09 and 2026-08-24 - CFO Matteo Tarditi moved to President/COO, Louis Martin to Chief Commercial Officer, external hire Alfredo Luchini (ex-Carrier) became CFO on 2026-08-10, Chief Supply Chain Officer Mark Bushway exits 2027-01-01, and Chief Corporate Affairs Officer Matthew Echols ceased to serve on 2026-08-24 - so a CFO four weeks into the seat delivers UNFI's first multi-year guide, and the Echols departure was disclosed only in an exit Form 4 with no 8-K and no press release.
why_not_priced: The Echols exit exists only as a Form 4 with no transactions and a single footnote, filed 2026-08-27 - there is no press release and no 8-K item 5.02 for it, so no news aggregator, no Zacks note and no wire preview carries it, and the count of C-suite changes is therefore understated everywhere the market looks. On the guide itself: with two published FY27 estimates there is no consensus number visible against which a conservative first guide could already be marked, so 'new CFO resets the base' cannot be in the price the way it would be on a twenty-analyst name, where you would see a pre-print estimate cut cluster. What holds this finding down, and why the band crosses zero, is that the print was pulled forward roughly three weeks from the late-September/early-October date UNFI used in each of the prior three years (last year's Q4 release was 2025-09-30), landing 38 days after fiscal year end - reporting early with a month-old CFO argues for a clean, confident close rather than a reset.
independence: A second, separate SEC document: the exit Form 4 for Matthew T Echols, period 2026-08-24, filed 2026-08-27 - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1020859/000162828026059263/0001628280-26-059263-index.htm. This is a different filing from the July 8-K but the same theme, so the two should collapse to one source cluster.

finding: Canaan's self-mining run-rate halved entering Q3 while it reported installed hashrate as flat: monthly BTC produced went 90 (April) / 90 (May) / 64 (June) / 46 (July) = 3.00 / 2.90 / 2.13 / 1.48 BTC per day, a 51% per-day decline, driven by Ethiopia (4.96 EH/s, a third of the 14.9 EH/s installed fleet) falling from 2.33 EH/s operating at 30 April to 0.36 EH/s at 30 June and then being described as 'paused' at 31 July -- yet the July release counted the entire paused 4.96 EH/s inside its headline 'operating computing power' of 14.24 EH/s, one month after the same table had shown Ethiopia at 0.36 EH/s operating.
why_not_priced: Reported Q2 mining volume (90+90+64 = 244 BTC vs 257 in Q1) will look almost flat, so the deterioration is invisible in the quarter being reported and only shows up in the Q3-to-date commentary and any Q3 guide. If the market had underwritten it, the stock would not have risen 68% in the 20 sessions that straddle the 17 August release of the 46-BTC month; the two named drivers of that rally were the 20 August Trump/CLARITY Act crypto bid and the 25-27 August Bitcoin Asia conference, i.e. sector beta and a trade show. Coverage is two EPS estimates and a 'Strong Buy' consensus with a $1.72 target on a $0.36 stock, so nobody is modelling site-level uptime. The August production 6-K, on the company's own mid-month cadence (April update 14 May, May update 11 June, June update 14 July, July update 17 August), falls after the 8 September print, so the print is the first place an August number or an Ethiopia explanation can surface.
independence: CryptoSlate, 2026-08-19, independently flagged that 4.96 EH/s of paused Ethiopian capacity sat inside the 14.24 EH/s operating total and that June 30 had shown Ethiopia at only 0.36 EH/s operating: https://cryptoslate.com/canaan-counted-paused-ethiopia-mining-as-nearly-35-of-its-july-operating-hashrate-total/ . Separate context, and dated 2025 not 2026, so used only as background: Ethiopian Electric Power's CEO said on 7 August 2025 there would be 'no new contracts in the field of data mining, and we are not interested in continuing with existing ones either' (https://www.cryptopolitan.com/ethiopian-electric-power-to-phase-out-mining/). The June and July hashrate tables come from two different 6-K exhibits (accessions 0001104659-26-083490 filed 2026-07-14 and 0001104659-26-097615 filed 2026-08-17) but I am treating the disclosure inconsistency and the production decline as ONE finding, not two, because they rest on the same document pair.

finding: Canaan converted its automatic shelf into a $270m standard Form F-3 on 15 April 2026 specifically because it 'expects that it will cease to be a well-known seasoned issuer' on filing its FY2025 20-F, then filed Post-Effective Amendment No. 5 on 15 June 2026 as an 'exhibits-only filing to file an updated auditor consent' -- i.e. it is actively keeping a shelf equal to roughly its entire market value usable -- against cash that fell from US$80.8m at 31 December 2025 to US$43.5m at 31 March 2026, a Q1 gross LOSS of US$22.9m, US$21.1m short-term debt, and zero 424B5 takedowns anywhere in 2026 after three in 2025 (March, October, November).
why_not_priced: An exhibits-only post-effective amendment to refresh an auditor consent generates no headline, no wire story and no aggregator row -- it is pure plumbing whose only purpose is to keep the shelf sellable, and it is not in the +68% run-up. If the market were pricing takedown risk you would see it in the skew, and there is no two-sided ATM option chain here at all. The specific asymmetry is timing: after ten months without using the shelf while burning ~US$37m of cash in a single quarter, the first 68% rally in a year is the first usable equity window, and a pre-open results release with an 8:00 a.m. call is where issuers of this type disclose one.
independence: Points the same way but from a different document: the 4 August 2026 buyback release funds repurchases by monetising the digital asset treasury rather than from cash, and states Canaan held ~US$130m of digital assets as of 3 August -- consistent with cash being the constrained resource (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1780652/000110465926090114/tm2622168d1_ex99-1.htm, 2026-08-04). Honest counterweight from that same document: a company that announced a buyback five weeks ago is less likely to price an offering, which is why I size this small. A screener figure of 744.84m shares outstanding as of 4 September (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/can/) sits above the 690,594,191 ADSs the company reported at 31 March 2026, but I could not confirm that from a primary filing and do not rely on it.

finding: There is a mid-June 2026 open-market insider buy cluster that is essentially invisible for this name because Canaan is a 20-F/6-K filer whose officers nonetheless file Section 16 forms: CFO Cheng Jin bought 65,000 ADSs at US$0.35 on 15 June, and CEO Nangeng Zhang bought 250,000 ADSs at US$0.34 on 17 June and 250,000 at US$0.33 on 18 June, and no insider has filed any transaction since 22 June -- no sales at all into the 68% rally.
why_not_priced: Insider-transaction screens and the sell-side notes on this name are built around the FPI assumption that a 20-F filer has no Section 16 reporting at all, so these Form 4s are not in any Canaan coverage I could find; had they been picked up, a CEO buying half a million ADSs three days before the low would have generated at least one wire story, and it generated none. It is also stale by twelve weeks and the purchase prices (US$0.33-0.35) sit essentially at today's US$0.36, which is exactly why I size it under one point rather than treating it as a signal about the print.
independence: Separate filer, separate accession, same direction: the CEO's own Form 4 for 17-18 June at US$0.34 and US$0.33 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1780652/000180299326000005/form4-06222026_040601.xml, filed 2026-06-22). Distinct from finding 2's documents.

finding: Canaan is inside its second and final Nasdaq minimum-bid-price compliance period, expiring 11 January 2027, with the ADSs at US$0.36 -- needing roughly +178% and then ten consecutive closes at or above US$1.00 -- and the company has committed to nothing more than that it 'will evaluate all available options during the second compliance period to rectify the deficiency'; I found no depositary notice of any Canaan reverse split or ADS-ratio change, and an ADS-ratio change (currently 1 ADS = 15 Class A shares) needs no shareholder vote and can be effected in weeks.
why_not_priced: The deficiency itself IS in the wire and is priced; what is not priced is that with about four months and one earnings call left, the 8 September pre-open release is the natural and cheapest venue to announce a ratio change, and the company has so far declined to name the remedy. If the market had positioned for it there would be visible put demand -- instead the chain has no two-sided ATM legs at all and put/call open interest is 0.03, i.e. essentially no downside protection outstanding. I sized this at only one point because it is a mechanical, disclosed clock rather than new information.
independence: Negative check rather than confirmation: the two 2026 depositary reverse-split notices that a search for Canaan surfaced turn out to be for NIP Group Inc. (effective 6 July 2026, https://depositaryreceipts.citi.com/adr/common/file.aspx?idf=7873, notice dated 2026-06-15) and Nobia AB (effective 22 May 2026, https://depositaryreceipts.citi.com/adr/common/file.aspx?idf=7817, notice dated 2026-05-12) -- neither is Canaan, so no Canaan ratio action has been noticed to holders as of today.

finding: Cipher Mining's 53,762,660 CAN ADSs (806,439,900 Class A shares, ~9.2% of the 585.8m reported float), issued to it at US$0.7394/ADS on 2026-02-23 as payment for the ABC Projects JV stake, came out of lock-up on 2026-08-23 -- Cipher's own 10-Q states the date and carries the position inside 'Prepaid expenses and other current assets', and the shares were never registered for resale, so Cipher can sell under Rule 144 as a non-affiliate with no volume cap and no Form 144 trail.
why_not_priced: The block is invisible to every screen that quotes this name: stockanalysis.com's float of 585.80m excludes it, Canaan's own EDGAR filer index shows no Schedule 13G or 13D from Cipher (CIK 1819989) among the 13Gs on file, Canaan filed no resale registration for it (the 2026-05-22 POS AM to F-3 333-285125 is a $270m primary shelf and names no selling shareholder), and Cipher as a non-affiliate owes no Form 144. If the market had done the arithmetic you would see (a) FY27 EPS estimates cut on the share-count line, because a $1.5bn programme executed on the prior 18-month cadence implies ~20m shares / ~5% of the count retired and the actual count is going nowhere (420.4m weighted diluted FY26, 412.5m in Q4 FY26, ~409.8m outstanding now), (b) the capital-return leg stripped out of bull cases, and (c) the option skew bid for downside rather than -3.35 vol points the other way. Tomorrow's 10-Q Item 5 issuer-purchase table and the diluted share count make the Q1 number explicit for the first time: roughly 250k shares / ~$19m repurchased in a quarter in which the company also closed $650m of Reliant and raised $1.2bn of notes.
independence: A different document points the same way: the FY26 Q4 press release (SEC 8-K exhibit) gives no free cash flow guidance for FY27 at all, while guiding gross rental capex UP to $2.45-2.85bn — Ashtead's practice under the old reporting regime was to give and even raise FCF guidance (it raised FY26 FCF guidance at the Q1 print on 3 Sept 2025). https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002083785/000162828026044797/sunbeltpressrelease-fy26q4.htm and https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/ashtead-q1-fy26-slides-rental-revenue-up-24-raises-free-cash-flow-guidance-93CH-4220646 . The weekly repurchase notices (detail/100, detail/122, detail/137, detail/155, detail/157 and the 2 June 2026 notice) are one source cluster and should be collapsed to one; the treasury-share balances and the per-week share counts inside them are two readings of the same filings, not independent evidence.

URI is down 13.2% over the past month from an all-time-high close on 17 Aug and sits at $1,014.46 against a 52-week high of $1,179.18, i.e. -14.0% from its high on the same tape and the same macro (the 4 Sept hot payrolls print lifted rate-hike odds and hit cyclicals). independence: Separate source, separate company: United Rentals' own Q2 2026 release (22 July 2026) https://investors.unitedrentals.com/press-releases/press-releases-details/2026/United-Rentals-Announces-Record-Second-Quarter-Results-and-Raises-Full-Year-2026-Guidance/default.aspx and Herc's Q2 2026 release via ARA's Rental Management https://news.ararental.org/herc-reports-q2-2026-results-increases-full-year-guidance ; the URI price/52-week-high anchor is https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/uri/ . finding: Edge Retail Academy's US independent-jeweler panel shows the category decelerating sharply in August 2026 — gross sales +5% YoY (vs +18% in June and +10% in July), units -8%, average retail sale +14% — with the opening-price-point sterling silver / alternative metals category at -5% dollars and -19% units; August is month one of Signet's fiscal Q3 and the month the H2 guide has to be built on.
why_not_priced: The Edge series is published in jewelry trade press (JCK, InStore, Edge's own blog) five days before the print and is not carried by any financial wire, terminal or aggregator; Signet has only ~3 EPS estimates on the tape, so there is no sell-side machine converting a trade-press monthly into a Q3 comp. If it were priced, the 25-delta skew would not be -13.46 vol points (calls bid over puts) and Citi would not have opened a public 'upside 30-day catalyst watch' on 2026-09-08 expecting a raise to the top end of the range. The same series was benign through the quarter itself (+12/+18/+10 in May/Jun/Jul), so this is specifically a forward-guide signal, not a restatement of the Q2 print. Note the level is not transferable — Edge ran +12% in April while Signet comped +1.8% in Q1 — the sequential shape is the signal, and it is a ~7pt one-month deceleration.
independence: Two different sources point the same way on the value-end consumer: PROG Holdings' Q2 2026 call named jewelry as one of only two categories at Purchasing Power that failed to grow GMV year over year (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/07/prog-prg-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/), and Pandora's calendar-Q2 2026 report showed North America like-for-like negative with US sales only 'stable' (https://wwd.com/accessories-news/jewelry/pandora-q2-results-2026-guidance-raised-early-announcement-1239092531/). The May/June/July Edge readings come from the same source cluster as this finding and are deliberately folded into it rather than filed separately.

finding: The 15% Section 122 global import surcharge that underpinned Signet's 'mid-teens effective tariff rate for the year' expired 12:01am on 2026-07-24 and was replaced the same minute by Section 301 forced-labor duties of 10%–12.5% on the 60 economies covering Signet's sourcing base — a 2.5–5 point step down on India, the country Signet named as its principal tariff exposure, four days before its quarter ended and seven weeks after the FY27 guide was set.
why_not_priced: This is a macro trade-law event that lands in the index, not in SIG's relative price; converting it requires knowing the specific sentence in Signet's 2026-06-02 call ('mid-teens effective tariff rate for the year') and that the guide was built on the 15% Section 122 number. With three estimates on the tape there is no published model of Signet's tariff line to revise. If it were priced you would see a tariff-relief note among the handful of SIG previews; instead the only visible preview thesis is Citi's generic 'inline Q2, raise to the top end', which is about demand, not landed cost. Slow-burning: Signet's ~$2.0bn inventory against ~$4bn COGS means post-July-24 landings mostly hit Q4/Q1 P&L, which is why I size it small.
independence: Jewelry-specific confirmation of the rates and effective date from National Jeweler (https://nationaljeweler.com/articles/15165-new-trump-tariffs-what-they-mean-for-jewelry), which puts India/China/Thailand/HK/UAE at 12.5% and Canada/Mexico/Pakistan/Sri Lanka/UK at 10% — note it disagrees with a 10% figure reported for India elsewhere, so I treat the step-down as 2.5–5 points rather than a point estimate. This finding and the refund finding below share the tariff theme but rest on different documents (a USTR action versus Signet's own disclosure); they should be collapsed to one residual if scored as a cluster.

finding: Signet has filed IEEPA refund claims on most goods where it was importer of record and had received only 'a small amount' as of 2026-06-02, with management stating it is too early to quantify the amount or timing 'as well as how any proceeds may be used' — meaning the FY27 guide contains none of it, while CBP had already built out mass electronic IEEPA refunds covering ~82% of affected entries by April 2026, i.e. during Signet's Q2.
why_not_priced: The item is knowably excluded from guidance by the company's own words, and it is unquantifiable from outside — which is exactly why no estimate carries it and why the wire preview cannot contain it. The 'how any proceeds may be used' phrasing is a buyback tell: Signet has $355m remaining on the 2017 authorisation after a $50m ASR on 2026-06-08 and had $602.8m cash / ~$1.7bn liquidity at Q1, against a $3.2bn market cap. If the market were carrying this, the stock would not be at 8x the midpoint of a $9.20–$11.00 FY27 EPS guide and the put/call open interest ratio would not be 3.27. Wide band because the refund may land as a Q3 event, be excluded from adjusted EPS, or be deferred into contested CIT proceedings.
independence: The refund mechanism and its timing come from a different source entirely — Skadden's account of the post-Supreme-Court CBP refund process (https://www.skadden.com/insights/publications/2026/03/tariff-refund-mechanism-takes-shape) — and the buyback capacity from Signet's 2026-06-08 8-K item 8.01 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/832988/000083298826000161/sig-20260608.htm). Shares the tariff theme with the finding above; different documents.

finding: InnovAge's raised FY2026 guidance implies a Q4 adjusted EBITDA of only $14.7-19.7M (9M actual $70.3M = Q1 $17.6M + Q2 $22.2M + Q3 $30.495M, against a $85-90M full-year guide) and Q4 revenue of $222-247M versus Q3's $251.9M actual - i.e. a sequential revenue decline and a 4-5pp margin collapse - even though census rose to ~8,050, Colorado/state Medicaid rates are fixed through 30 June, Medicare risk scores are fixed for the calendar year, and the in-house pharmacy saving is structural; the identical structure in FY2025 (9M EBITDA $23.1M vs a $24-31M guide, implying Q4 of $0.9-7.9M) produced an actual Q4 of $11.3M and a full year of $34.5M, 11% above the top of guidance.

No sell-side note, article or transcript question has laid out the implied Q4 step-down - the Q3 call transcript records that no analyst pressed management on it and management declined to forecast Q4. If the market had done this arithmetic the stock would not be drifting -5.96% over 20 days into the print at exactly the $10 average analyst target; it would be marked up toward the $13 KeyBanc target set 2026-08-21.
independence: Nine-month revenue of $727.8M is confirmed independently in the 10-Q at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1834376/000183437626000022/innv-20260331.htm (filed 2026-05-08), and the Q1 FY26 $17.6M adjusted EBITDA anchor comes from a separate release at https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/11/04/3180867/0/en/InnovAge-Announces-Financial-Results-for-the-Fiscal-First-Quarter-Ended-September-30-2025.html (2025-11-04). The FY2025 precedent guide of $24-31M is from a different document again, https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/05/06/3075531/0/en/InnovAge-Announces-Financial-Results-for-the-Fiscal-Third-Quarter-Ended-March-31-2025.html (2025-05-06). finding: Colorado - InnovAge's home and largest state - enacted roughly $270M of Medicaid reimbursement cuts for FY2026-27, taking most fee-for-service rates down to 85% of Medicare from 2026-04-01 and layering a further 2.0% across-the-board reduction on HCBS waiver services for dates of service from 2026-07-01, published in the June 2026 provider bulletin after InnovAge last spoke to investors; PACE Medicaid capitation is set beneath an upper payment limit derived from exactly those FFS/HCBS costs, so the FY2027 Colorado rate InnovAge must build its first FY2027 guide around is flat-to-down rather than the mid-single-digit increases of prior years.
why_not_priced: The qualitative warning IS on the wire - the CFO said on 2026-05-06 that FY2027 Medicaid increases 'may be lower than what we have experienced historically' and the CEO guided Medicare to +1.5-2%. What is not on the wire is the mechanism or the size: no published note quantifies the 85%-of-Medicare reset or the 2% July-1 HCBS cut, and the July-1 piece was only confirmed in a state provider bulletin issued a month after InnovAge's last communication. If this were priced you would see a published FY2027 EBITDA estimate cut or a downgrade in the four months since the Q3 call; instead the only rated action on file is KeyBanc reiterating Buy with a $13 target on 2026-08-21 and the stock sits at the $10 average target.
independence: Independently corroborated by state budget reporting: https://www.cpr.org/2026/04/01/colorado-budget-draft-billion-shortfall-2026/ (2026-04-01, on the ~$1.5bn shortfall and the Medicaid-led cuts) and https://www.vaildaily.com/news/colorado-new-budget-cuts-medicaid/ on the signed budget. Directionally consistent with, but sourced separately from, management's own May commentary in https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/06/innovage-innv-q3-2026-earnings-transcript/ - that transcript is shared colour with finding 1 and should be collapsed to one source.

finding: Meta's own Q2 2026 release (2026-07-29, 57 days after ODDITY last guided) shows average price per ad +12% y/y -- identical to Q1 2026 -- with ad impressions growth decelerating from +19% to +14%, i.e. the auction ODDITY blames for its CPA blow-up is still inflating at an unchanged rate while inventory growth slows; ODDITY's whole Q2/H2 case rests on its 'largest advertising partner' delivering an estimated 40-60% CPA recovery through system fixes.

If the market had connected the two, the front-expiry 25-delta skew would not be at -16.19 vol points (calls bid over puts) on a name whose last two earnings reactions were -49% and -30%, and the stock would not be trading 21-32% above the $10.09-$11.07 consensus price target after a 36% rally off the 52-week low.
independence: Similarweb shows ilmakiage.com traffic still declining -4.73% month-over-month with display advertising still the single largest channel at 28.84% of visits -- i.e. no visible re-scaling of the paid funnel. https://www.similarweb.com/website/ilmakiage.com/ (read 2026-09-08). finding: On 2026-09-03 a single line -- the October 16 2026 $7.50 put -- printed 24,001 contracts, 99.9% of the day's total ODD options volume and 2.8x the entire pre-existing open interest of 8,509, at a strike 48.4% below the then-spot of $14.54; on the same day the 3-month 90/110 skew FELL 4.76 percentage points to 0.73, which is the direction skew moves when size is sold to dealers, not bought.

A market genuinely braced for a third leg down after -49% and -30% would show downside skew rising into the print and puts bid; instead the front expiry pays 16.19 vol points more for calls and a customer appears to have underwritten 2.4m shares of downside below $7.50. Treat this and finding 1 as ONE directional bet: finding 1 is the reason to lean down, this is only the reason the down-case pays more than symmetric. Do not add the two impacts.

finding: IL MAKIAGE's own web traffic -- whose single largest channel is Display advertising at 28.84% of desktop visits, i.e. a direct read on the paid-acquisition funnel management says it is re-scaling -- kept falling sequentially all summer: 2.44M visits in June 2026, 2.36M in July (-3.18%), ~2.3M in August (-4.73%), with the site's global rank sliding from ~10,747 to ~15,447 over three months.

Nobody aggregates brand-level traffic for ODD, there is no sell-side note or wire story on it, and if the market had checked it the coverage would not read 'Makes Progress Toward Normalization' and the 25-delta skew would not be -16 vol points bid for calls. Re-scaled acquisition spend produces rising sessions; sessions fell in each of the three months after the guide was given.
independence: Same-vendor family but a DIFFERENT property and a different month, acting as a seasonality control: spoiledchild.com traffic rose 3.95% month-over-month in August 2026 while ilmakiage.com fell 4.73% in the same month, so the IL MAKIAGE erosion is brand-specific rather than the summer beauty-DTC trough -- and IL MAKIAGE is precisely the brand management identified as the one hit by the ad-platform dislocation. https://www.similarweb.com/website/spoiledchild.com/ and https://www.similarweb.com/website/ilmakiage.com/ (both August 2026 data)

finding: Short interest is 6.58M shares, ~23% of a 28.1M share float with 6-9 days to cover, and it ROSE from ~6.00M a month earlier -- shorts added into the rally and into the print; the most parsimonious reading of the baseline's -16.19 vol-point 25-delta skew is a crowded short book buying OTM calls as gap protection, not the market making a bullish statement.
why_not_priced: Two things are visibly mis-set. First, the current wire copy on ODD short interest is stale: the marketbeat item search engines surface for 'ODD short interest' is at URL path /2025/09/ and quotes 6.32M falling to 4.76M and 15.4% of shares -- an August 2025 series being served as current, so the published number understates both the level and the direction. Second, if the -16.19 skew were a genuine directional market view rather than short-book hedging, you would not simultaneously see a 24,001-lot deep-OTM put print and a sell-side average target 17% below spot. The practical consequence is asymmetry, not direction: with 6-9 days to cover, any in-line-or-better Q2 against a guide the company set three months ago under near-zero visibility gets amplified upward.
independence: Different source, different instrument, and it points the opposite way to the skew: on 2026-09-02/03 a single trade of 24,001 October $7.50 puts printed -- 99.9% of the day's option volume and ~2.8x that strike's existing open interest -- with the stock at $14.54, i.e. real money paying for a sub-$7.50 tail. Note this is a second reading of the SAME options market as the skew figure in my finding, so treat the options evidence as one cluster. https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/oddity-tech-options-flow-signals-defensive-positioning-ahead-of-september-earnings-93CH-4888226 (2026-09-03)

finding: A 6-K filed 2026-06-12 discloses that on 2026-06-11 Oddity Finance LLC privately agreed to repurchase $50M face of its 0% Exchangeable Senior Notes due 2030 for $35M cash, closing 2026-06-17 and leaving $550M outstanding -- roughly a $15M pre-tax gain on extinguishment that lands in Q2 GAAP results and is not in the $0.1223 adjusted consensus, and it prices the company's own paper at ~70 cents in June.
why_not_priced: Only TipRanks and GuruFocus picked this up; it did not reach the mainstream wire or any earnings preview I could find, and the one estimate on the calendar is an adjusted number that by construction excludes the gain. Its bigger use is as a read on management intent: with ~$632M of cash and investments post-transaction, $167M left on the $200M share authorisation as of 2026-03-31, and both its equity and its own bonds trading distressed, a fresh or upsized capital-return announcement alongside the print is a live positive tail that no preview I found flags.
