independence: https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/oddity-tech-to-repurchase-50-million-of-exchangeable-notes-at-discount -- confirms the same transaction from a non-EDGAR source, which is also the evidence that coverage was thin. The Q1 release's $667.4M cash/investments and $167M remaining authorisation come from the company's own 2026-06-02 exhibit: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1907085/000110465926069208/tm2615689d1_ex99-1.htm

finding: The US$10m buyback that drove the stock +21.5% on 2026-09-03 and anchored the +76% five-session run is 17 Education's sixth consecutive annual US$10m authorisation (Nov 2021, Sep 2022, Sep 2023, Sep 2024, Sep 2025, Sep 2026) and is a straight rollover of the identical US$10m program that ran 2025-09-04 to 2026-09-04 and expired four days before this one started.
why_not_priced: The 2026-09-03 release makes no reference to any prior program, and the identical predecessor was buried inside the 2025-09-04 Q2 earnings 6-K rather than issued as its own headline. Volume on 2026-09-03 was 2,789,500 ADS against a 20-day median of 4,600 before the event - a ~600x spike in a 10.86m-ADS name with no sell-side coverage and no option chain. If the market had recognised this as an expiring-program rollover rather than new capital, the tape would show a low-volume drift, not a 600x-volume +21.5% day followed by three more up sessions on no news at all; and the stock would not still be adding +18% intraday on 2026-09-08 on roughly average volume with nothing in the wire since 2026-09-03.
independence: Independent primary confirmation of the recurrence pattern from four separate filings, none of which is the 2026 release: the 2023-09-21 6-K authorising US$10m from 2023-11-02 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000095017023049313/yq-6k-09-22-2023.htm), the 2022-09-29 6-K authorising US$10m from 2022-11-02 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312522254314/d300245d6k.htm), the 2021-11-02 announcement of US$10m (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2021/11/02/2325327/0/en/17-Education-Technology-Group-Inc-Announces-US-10-Million-Share-Repurchase-Program-and-Plan-to-Implement-ADS-Ratio-Change.html), and the 2025-09-04 Q2 2025 release carrying the immediately-preceding US$10m authorisation (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000095017025112952/yq-ex99_1.htm). The FY2025 20-F's XBRL tagging separately names ShareRepurchaseProgramInSeptemberTwoThousandAndTwentyFourMember and ...TwentyFiveMember (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821468/000119312526191472/yq-20251231.htm).

finding: Q1 2026's headline RMB99.5m revenue (+359% YoY) was drawn largely out of a one-off pre-sale balance rather than new demand: deferred revenue and advances from customers fell from RMB165.9m at 2025-12-31 to RMB104.5m at 2026-03-31, a RMB61.5m drawdown equal to 62% of the quarter's revenue, and cash plus term deposits fell RMB54.6m (RMB406.9m to RMB352.3m) against a reported net loss of only RMB19.4m - 2.8x the loss.
why_not_priced: There is no sell-side model on a US$37.4m-market-cap name, no consensus estimate published, and every piece of wire copy on the quarter carried only the two lines the company led with - '+359.0% year-over-year' and 'Yiqi Aixue revenue more than quadrupled'. The Q1 earnings call had no Q&A at all (the operator recorded no questions), so the drawdown was never put to management. Had the market modelled the unwind, a stock at 0.73x its own liquid assets would not need a recurring buyback authorisation to re-rate 76%; the re-rating is being justified by the growth narrative, which is precisely the thing the deferred-revenue line qualifies. The remaining RMB104.5m balance also caps how much of this can repeat.
independence: The year-ago control comes from a DIFFERENT filing and shows the drawdown is not seasonal: in Q1 2025 deferred revenue fell only RMB40.4m to RMB36.9m, i.e. RMB3.5m or 16% of that quarter's RMB21.7m revenue, versus 62% this year, and cash plus deposits fell RMB25.9m against a LARGER net loss of RMB30.9m - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000095017025084635/yq-ex99_1.htm (2025-06-11). The Q4/FY2025 release shows where the balance came from - RMB40.4m at 2024-12-31 and RMB36.5m at 2025-09-30 building to RMB165.9m at 2025-12-31 on pre-sales of the new consumer product: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312526122709/yq-ex99_1.htm (2026-03-25) and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312525313418/yq-ex99_1.htm (2025-12-10). NOTE: the RMB61.5m deferred-revenue drawdown and the RMB54.6m cash decline are two readings of the same Q1 2026 document and are filed here as one finding, not two.

finding: The company dismissed Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu as its auditor effective 2026-05-27 and appointed Marcum Asia CPAs LLP for the year ending 2026-12-31 - i.e. it dropped a Big Four auditor two quarters after its revenue recognition profile changed beyond recognition, and the Q2 2026 numbers about to be released are the first reported under the new firm.
why_not_priced: It was disclosed in a 6-K with no press release and no GlobeNewswire distribution - it does not appear in the company's news feed alongside the buyback, the earnings date or the Q1 results, and the stock's reaction that day was -4.0%. It is a dismissal initiated by the company, not a resignation, with no disagreements or reportable events cited, so there is no headline to attach it to. If the market had weighted it, a name that just re-rated 76% on a boilerplate buyback would not be paying up for the same audited growth story; the coverage would carry a governance qualifier and it carries none.
independence: Points the same way as, but is documented separately from, the revenue-quality finding above (different filing, different date, different subject matter). No third-party source independently flags it - no analyst, ratings agency or short report on this name was found.

finding: Deferred revenue and advances from customers fell from RMB165.9m at 31-Dec-2025 to RMB104.5m at 31-Mar-2026, so RMB61.4m of the RMB99.5m of Q1 revenue that produced the headline '+359% YoY' was a drawdown of Q4 2025 pre-sale orders: implied new billings were only about RMB38m, less than the RMB43.2m spent on sales and marketing in the same quarter, and cash plus restricted cash plus term deposits fell RMB54.6m (RMB407.0m to RMB352.4m) against a reported net loss of just RMB19.4m.
why_not_priced: The wire copy on this quarter is 'AI learning app lifts 17EdTech revenue 359%, net loss down 37.4%' — headline growth and headline loss. The deferred-revenue line sits in the condensed balance sheet at the back of the same release and nobody has subtracted it: no sell-side analyst publishes an estimate on YQ, stockanalysis.com's news feed carries only the three headline items, and the release contains no cash-flow statement so the RMB54.6m cash decline versus a RMB19.4m loss has to be computed by differencing two balance sheets. If this were priced, the stock would not have closed the entire discount to book — shareholders' equity of RMB269.1m (US$39.0m) at 31-Mar-2026 against a US$37.5m market cap at $3.45 puts YQ at roughly 1.0x a book value that is falling about RMB18m a quarter, i.e. the deep-value cushion that justified the whole run has already gone. With only RMB104.5m of deferred balance left, the Q2 release's own deferred-revenue and cash lines are where this becomes visible for a second consecutive quarter.
independence: Chinese trade coverage independently describes the Q4 2025 launch as a membership product sold on pre-orders ('achieved strong pre-sale orders'), which is the mechanism: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312526122709/yq-ex99_1.htm (2026-03-25). Separately, Tencent News coverage of 2026-07-12 attributes the growth to a To-B/To-G 'smart paper-pen + AI' school solution covering 2,000+ schools rather than to the consumer app the English release credits, which is a second, unrelated reason to doubt the revenue narrative: https://news.qq.com/rain/a/20260712A066GD00. Note the RMB61.4m, RMB38m and RMB54.6m figures all come from the single Q1 6-K exhibit and are one finding, not three.

finding: The US$10 million buyback authorisation announced 2026-09-03 that triggered the +21.5% jump is at least the fourth identical US$10 million 12-month authorisation the company has issued (November 2021, September 2024, September 2025, September 2026), and the FY2024 20-F discloses that only approximately US$0.1 million had actually been repurchased under the September 2024 programme as of 31-Dec-2024 — about 1% of the authorisation.
why_not_priced: Volume on the announcement day was 2,789,500 ADSs against a 20-day pre-event median of 4,600 — a 600x spike. That is a buyer base that arrived on the headline, not one that pulled the 2024 20-F. If the recycling were priced, the third and fourth iterations of an identical press release would have produced no move at all, and the aggregator write-ups would say 'renews' rather than 'Approves $10M Share Buyback' and 'announces NEW share repurchase program'. The company also has RMB104.5m of deferred revenue and a RMB54.6m quarterly cash decline standing in front of the RMB71m the authorisation would cost, which is a capacity constraint the 2024 execution rate already demonstrated.
independence: The prior identical authorisations are documented in three separate places: the 2021 release at https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2021/11/02/2325327/0/en/17-Education-Technology-Group-Inc-Announces-US-10-Million-Share-Repurchase-Program-and-Plan-to-Implement-ADS-Ratio-Change.html (URL path confirms 2021, not 2026), the FY2024 20-F which contains the phrase 'repurchased approximately US$0.1 million' (single hit for this CIK on EDGAR full-text search) at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000095017025058824/yq-20241231.htm, and the FY2025 20-F whose inline-XBRL tags include 'ShareRepurchaseProgramInSeptemberTwoThousandAndTwentyFive' at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312526191472/yq-20251231.htm.

finding: Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu was dismissed as auditor effective 2026-05-27 — four weeks after signing the FY2025 20-F and three weeks before the Q1 revenue inflection was reported — and replaced by Marcum Asia CPAs LLP, a firm the PCAOB censured and fined US$100,000 on 2025-09-23.

There is no analyst coverage to write it up, the change was reported as a dismissal with no disagreements and no reportable events so it generated no wire story, and it has never been connected in print to the fact that the revenue line inflected 359% in the very quarter that straddles the change. Q2 is the first release published under the new engagement.
independence: PCAOB's own sanction release, an entirely separate source: https://pcaobus.org/news-events/news-releases/news-release-detail/pcaob-sanctions-u.s.-audit-firm-for-violations-related-to-communications-between-predecessor-and-successor-auditors (2025-09-23). A same-quarter CFO change points the same way — Sishi Zhou was confirmed as CFO on 2026-03-24 after nine months as Acting CFO: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312526120598/yq-ex99_1.htm.

finding: There is a real structural bid under the stock that cuts against the fade: the CEO's 10b5-1 plan runs to 31-Mar-2028 and the US$10m authorisation is live, against a non-Liu share base of only about 6.4m ADS-equivalent (542.2m shares outstanding less Andy Chang Liu's 223.9m / 41.30%) and a pre-spike median volume of 4,600 ADSs a day.
why_not_priced: The float arithmetic requires combining the 13D/A percentages with the 20-F share count, and no aggregator does it: stockanalysis.com reports 10.86m shares outstanding and a US$37.45m market cap with no float adjustment at all. A stock where 41.3% is held by one person and baseline turnover is 4,600 ADSs a day cannot absorb even partial execution of a US$10m programme without gapping, so the downside from the four negative findings above is genuinely dampened relative to what the fundamentals alone would imply — which is why my net number is -9.5 and not the -11.5 the negatives sum to.
independence: Share count from the FY2025 20-F cover: 'As of December 31, 2025, there were 542,229,838 ordinary shares outstanding' — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312526191472/yq-20251231.htm (2026-04-29). Market cap and 10.86m ADS from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/yq/ (2026-09-08). Shares its source document with the 10b5-1 finding above and is the opposite-signed reading of it.

finding: Navan's Q2 FY27 revenue guide of $219-221m is flat sequentially on Q1's $220m, but the company's only observable prior year grew +9.6% sequentially over the same fiscal quarters (Q1 FY26 $157.1m -> Q2 FY26 $172.2m, derivable from the disclosed 9M FY26 revenue of $524.3m less Q3 FY26 of $195m, and cross-checked by the stated 40% and 28% YoY growth rates); consensus of $220.5m is the guide midpoint to within $0.5m, so the street has not applied that seasonality at all.
why_not_priced: If the street had modelled last year's shape it would carry ~$230-241m for Q2, not $220.5m. Consensus landing inside the guide band by half a million dollars is the visible fingerprint of guide-anchoring on a company with only four public quarters and no consensus seasonality template. Had it been priced, the option-implied move would not need to be 14% and the 25d skew would not be +5.64 vol points paid for downside into a print the sell-side has raised targets into three times in three weeks.
independence: The Q2 revenue guide and the Q1 FY27 base come from a different document, the 2026-06-10 8-K exhibit https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1639723/000162828026042206/exhibit991-earningspressre.htm ; the $220.5m consensus figure comes from a third source, Oppenheimer's 2026-08-27 preview at https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/oppenheimer-raises-navan-stock-price-target-on-ai-gains-travel-growth-93CH-4878997

finding: The price half of Navan's gross bookings accelerated sharply across its fiscal Q2 (May-Jul 2026): US CPI airline fares ran +26.7%, +26.5% and +25.5% YoY in May/Jun/Jul against +7.1%, +14.9% and +20.7% in Feb/Mar/Apr, its fiscal Q1 -- roughly a 12pp step-up -- while consensus gross bookings of $2.86bn implies a 7.7% sequential DECLINE from Q1's $3.1bn, versus a roughly +1% sequential move in the same fiscal quarters a year earlier.
why_not_priced: Gross bookings is Navan's headline KPI and it is a dollar figure, so it mechanically inherits fare inflation; nobody maps the BLS air-fare series onto a fiscal quarter that runs May-July. If it were priced, previews would frame the quarter on booking VALUE rather than on client wins and AI engagement, and consensus bookings growth would not be set 13pp below the prior quarter's realised 50% exactly as the price input doubled. The downside tail in my range is the same fact read the other way: per-transaction supplier fees do not scale with fare, so usage revenue/GBV -- already down from 6.92% to 6.52% YoY in Q1 -- compresses further, giving bears a visible take-rate deterioration alongside a flattering bookings headline.
independence: Corroborated by an independent demand read: Amex GBT reported Q2 2026 transaction growth of 45% and TTV growth of 57% on 2026-08-04 (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260804630662/en/American-Express-Global-Business-Travel-Reports-Strong-Q2-2026-Financial-Results), and STR/CoStar put July 2026 US hotel RevPAR +8.2% with ADR +5.7% (https://www.costar.com/products/str-benchmark/resources/press-releases/us-hotel-performance-july-2026). Caveat that cuts against: GBTA's July 2026 corporate forecast has global business airfares up only 4.7% for the year, so negotiated corporate fares travel far less than retail CPI. The take-rate reading in the last sentence shares the Q1 FY27 release with finding 1 and should be collapsed into this finding, not counted twice.

finding: The 12% drawdown from the 2026-08-27 all-time high is at least partly mechanical post-lock-up insider supply, not a fundamental de-rating: CEO Ariel Cohen sold 168,378 shares directly plus 75,000 through each of three GST trusts at $30.1441 on 08-27 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-01-06, alongside a cluster of five Form 4s filed 08-24 and four Form 144s filed 08-27.
why_not_priced: The baseline's two bearish inputs -- run_up_20d of -7.19% and a +5.64 vol-point put skew -- are being read as information. A 10b5-1 plan adopted in January cannot contain a view on a quarter that ended in July, so the supply is uninformative, and the drawdown into the print is weaker bear evidence than a -7% run-up normally is. If the market had decoded this, the pre-print drift would not have gone the opposite way to three consecutive target raises (TD Cowen $29->$34 on 08-17, Oppenheimer $30->$35 on 08-27, BofA $26->$34 on 09-02).
independence: Separate confirmation of the target-raise sequence and the drawdown from a non-EDGAR source: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/navn/ (accessed 2026-09-09, shows the 08-17, 08-27 and 09-02 raises and a $26.63 price against the 08-27 high).

finding: US airline-fare CPI averaged +26.2% y/y across May-July 2026 (Navan's fiscal Q2) versus +14.2% y/y across Feb-April 2026 (fiscal Q1), and the seasonally-adjusted index rose 6.4% sequentially between those two windows (291.3 avg to 310.0 avg) — a ~12pp step-up in the dollar-price tailwind to gross booking volume inside the quarter management guided to 28% revenue growth, down 12pp from Q1's 40%.
why_not_priced: Navan's revenue is a take rate on booking dollars, so ticket-price inflation flows through GBV and usage revenue almost mechanically, yet no preview maps a macro CPI series onto a Feb-Jan fiscal calendar — the Q1/Q2 split (Feb-Apr vs May-Jul) is not a calendar quarter and the step-up is invisible unless you cut the series that way. If it were priced you would not see the stock down 7.19% over 20 days and 25-delta skew at +5.64 vol points into a print where the guided revenue growth rate falls by exactly as much as the price tailwind rose; you would see call skew and a run-up.
independence: Delta's CEO on 2026-07-10 said higher airfares would persist and reported corporate travel up in the June quarter with record corporate sales (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/10/delta-air-lines-dal-q2-2026-earnings.html); BofA separately modelled United Q3 unit revenue +15.6% on 'price hikes working their way through the booking curve' (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/bofa-sees-delta-united-entering-191300683.html). Amex GBT, the same demand pool, reported transactions +45% and TTV +57% on 2026-08-04 and reiterated FY guidance (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260804630662/en/American-Express-Global-Business-Travel-Reports-Strong-Q2-2026-Financial-Results). Partial offset from the same BLS release: lodging away from home fell 2.8% m/m in July and the lodging index dropped from 195.7 in May to 185.9 in July, so the hotel leg of GBV is roughly flat-to-down sequentially — I have netted that into the sizing.

finding: Navan's Q2 FY27 guide of $219-221m implies exactly 0% sequential revenue growth off Q1's $220m, whereas the same fiscal quarter a year earlier grew +9.1% sequentially ($157.5m to $171.9m); repeating last year's own seasonality would put Q2 at roughly $240m, i.e. +40% y/y — the same growth rate Navan just printed — against a guide of +28%.
why_not_priced: The Q2 FY26 revenue base is not in any wire recap: Navan has never reported a standalone Q2 as a public company (it IPO'd 2025-10-30), so $171.9m only exists as a subtraction of the Q1 FY26 comparative in the Q1 FY27 release from the six-month figure buried in the S-1. Previews therefore anchor on the y/y guide rate rather than on the sequential shape, and management's stated rationale — a 'seasonally slightly weaker summer season' — is contradicted by the company's own prior-year seasonality, which was seasonally stronger. If the market had done this arithmetic the guide would be treated as a floor and the stock would not be trading below where the CEO's 10b5-1 plan sold nine sessions ago.
independence: Arithmetically self-verifying against a second document: the S-1 gives six-month FY26 revenue of $329.413m (usage $299.698m + subscription $29.715m) at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1639723/000162828025042130/navan-sx1.htm ; $329.413m less the $157.5m Q1 FY26 comparative is $171.9m, and $220m / $171.9m is 28.0%, which reproduces the company's stated Q2 guide growth rate exactly. If the read-across were priced, consensus would not still be modelling a YoY decline and the FY Street number would not sit at $2.23 against a company guide of $2.00-$2.20. The unpriced part is not the beat — it is the reaction function: at -15.7 vol points of skew the option market is paying up for calls into a catalyst whose two nearest analogues, three and four weeks ago, produced -3.5% and -0.1% because both were punished on the top line while the one-time gain was discounted entirely. Second-order risk in the same cluster and pointing the same way: the CIT's July order gives a confirmed refund path only to importers that sued, Macy's is not identifiable among the CIT plaintiffs and its own language was that 'timing and amounts remain uncertain' — so Macy's may book materially less than the ~$0.24 Jefferies has publicly penciled in, or nothing, while peers banked theirs.
independence: Dillard's 8-K/release of 2026-08-13 quantifies the same catalyst independently at $37.2m ($1.82/share) with the stock closing down ~3.5% that day: https://investor.dillards.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dillards-inc-reports-second-quarter-and-year-date-results-3 . Separately, Holland & Knight (2026-07-27) documents that non-plaintiff importers have no confirmed refund path: https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2026/07/file-now-cits-order-confirms-only-importers-that-have-sued . These are different documents from the Kohl's 8-K but sit in one tariff-refund source cluster with it — treat as one finding, not three.

finding: Kewaunee ran a book-to-bill of roughly 0.83 for all of FY26 -- consolidated backlog fell $214.6m -> $205.0m -> $192.9m -> $183.2m -> $165.9m across five straight quarters (an accelerating burn, -$17.3m in Q4 alone) while quarterly revenue was held flat at $71.1m / $70.1m / $69.4m / $71.4m -- and the FY26 10-K states 'not less than 90% of our order backlog at April 30, 2026 will be shipped during fiscal year 2027', i.e. >=$149m of shipments from backlog against $282m of FY26 revenue; with FY26 opex of $63.7m (~$15.9m/quarter, largely fixed) and a 28.5% gross margin, breakeven revenue is ~$56m per quarter, so Q1 FY27 revenue anywhere in the $55-63m range against the $71.1m year-ago comp puts EPS near zero versus $1.04.
why_not_priced: If this arithmetic were priced there would be a published FY27 revenue estimate below $240m and a sell-side note on the operating-leverage cliff; instead stockanalysis.com shows 'Analyst Forecast: Not available', the sweep found a single estimate, there is no conference call and no option chain, and the stock trades ~2,000 shares a day (368 shares today). Most tellingly, the 2026-06-23 release that disclosed the single largest backlog drop of the cycle produced only a -3.63% reaction, versus -21.23% and -13.08% on prior, smaller backlog disappointments -- that is not a market that has run the conversion math. And the stock at $36.01 is 11.2x trailing $3.22, which is not a multiple that embeds an EPS collapse.
independence: The backlog chain comes from four separate 8-K exhibits rather than one document: Q1 FY26 ($205.0m) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/55529/000005552925000033/prfy26q1earningsrelease.htm , Q2 FY26 ($192.9m) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/55529/000005552925000051/prfy26q2earningsrelease.htm , Q3 FY26 ($183.2m) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/55529/000005552926000006/prfy26q3earningsrelease.htm , Q4 FY26 ($165.9m, LPG $118.8m / International $47.1m) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/55529/000005552926000017/prfy26q4earningsrelease.htm . finding: Building Q2 FY27 revenue bottom-up from Wealthfront's own published monthly assets (May: cash $45.0bn / advisory $54.0bn; June: cash $44.8bn / advisory $54.3bn) at the company's own last-reported annualised take rates (cash 0.58%, advisory 0.21%) gives ~$94.5m even assuming July was flat with June, versus a sell-side consensus near $98.0m and an FY27 consensus of $384.9m that requires ~$98m in each remaining quarter.

finding: Adobe must guide Q4 net-new Digital Media ARR on this call with the president of the Creativity & Productivity business (David Wadhwani) having resigned effective 2026-09-27 with no named successor in the 8-K, an interim CFO (Steve Day) since June, and a CEO-elect from the enterprise/Digital Experience side who does not take office until 2026-12-01 - i.e. every person who owns or will own that number is either leaving or not yet in post.

The mechanical consequence is different and is not in any preview I found: the Q4 ARR bar is being set by an interim CFO and an outgoing CEO three weeks before the segment head walks and twelve weeks before a new CEO arrives, which is the textbook set-up for a de-risked guide rather than the 'beat-and-raise minimum' the previews say is required. If this were priced the 25-delta skew would not be -15.2 vol points (the most call-bid name in today's universe) and the preview copy would be arguing about who guides the number rather than about generative AI.

finding: Grocery dollar inflation is running materially hotter in Kroger's Q2 window than in the Q1 window that management extrapolated from: food-at-home CPI was +1.9% y/y in March 2026 but +2.7% y/y in each of May, June and July 2026, so Kroger's 'roughly in line with the first quarter' 1.0% identical-sales guide, set on 2026-06-18, embeds roughly 50-60bp less price than the quarter is actually carrying.
why_not_priced: This is the one leg that cuts upward and it is the reason the answer is -2.3 and not -4. It is public and free, but the previews all quote the EPS consensus rather than the comp, and Kroger's identical-sales line is the number this stock trades on. Management guided the comp on 2026-06-18 with only March and April CPI in hand; June and July food-at-home prints (both +2.7%) landed after. finding: Oracle has sold ZERO shares under its $20bn at-the-market common equity program: the FY2026 10-K tags 'Common stock shares sold' under the ATM Offering member as 0, and the FY2026 cash flow statement shows only $1,449m of common stock proceeds (ESPP/option exercises) against $4,954m of mandatory convertible preferred and $46,093m of notes/term loans - yet on 2026-06-23, one day after filing the 10-K, Oracle filed a 424B5 adding roughly ten further sales agents to that same $20bn program, and shares outstanding are still ~2.88bn (2,880,471,000 at 2026-06-12), so the whole ~127m-share, 4.4%-of-shares-out supply is still to come and the Q1 10-Q filed with this print is its first disclosure window.
why_not_priced: The February plan was received as financing solved - CDS tightened sharply the day it was announced (CNBC, 2026-02-02) - and since then the $20bn ATM has only ever been referenced as an intention inside the FY2027 '$40bn of debt and equity' line, never as unexecuted supply. If the market were pricing 127m shares of imminent issuance into this print you would not see a -7.35 vol-point call-bid skew, a 0.79 put/call open-interest ratio and a 37% rally off the 24-July level of $114.99 (the price stamped in Oracle's own 2026-07-28 Form 4) with the stock closing the gap back to where the Vice Chairman sold in late June at $156-165. Equity issuance is the one mechanism that mechanically caps an up-tail, and a company that has just recovered 37% and must fund ~$90-95bn of gross FY2027 capex against $31.98bn of operating cash flow has both the motive and, as of 23 June, the expanded distribution machinery to sell into strength immediately after this print. This is a cluster: the R70 tag, the R8 cash flow line and the R1 share count are three readings of one document (the FY2026 10-K) and should count once; the 424B5 agent expansion is the genuinely separate leg.
independence: The 2026-06-23 424B5 adding sales agents to the same program is a separate filing from the 10-K and is what you file before distributing size: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001341439/000119312526278585/d120346d424b5.htm . Separately, S&P's 2026-07-09 downgrade to BBB-/A-3 models FY2027 capex at $90-95bn versus its own prior $60bn forecast, which is the funding hole the equity leg exists to fill: https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/-/view/sourceId/101695609

finding: The Green Chile gas pipeline that is to fuel Project Jupiter - the Oracle/OpenAI Stargate campus in Dona Ana County, New Mexico that Oracle itself promoted on 2026-07-28 and that is designed around ~2.5GW of Bloom Energy gas fuel cells - has been pushed from 15 August 2026 to 1 February 2027 in an Energy Transfer/Transwestern filing, after the New Mexico State Land Office denied the route permit for a second time on water-use and emissions grounds.

why_not_priced: The revolver 8-K was never press-released — StockTitan's FEIM feed from June to September 2026 lists no June item at all, going straight from 27 May to 15 July — so a debt-free-for-decades company pledging all its assets for $10m mid-quarter never reached the wire. If the market had connected it to Q1 capacity, the 25-delta skew would not be sitting at +1.16 (essentially balanced) and the stock would not be up 7.7% in the five sessions into the print; instead the tape is treating the 20-day drawdown as pure post-offering supply.
independence: Independent confirmation of the $1.6m starting cash position and of the working-capital use of proceeds comes from two other documents: the Q4 FY2026 8-K release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/39020/000118518526002982/feimex99-1.htm, 2026-07-15) and the prospectus supplement's use-of-proceeds language 'capital expenditures, working capital and other general corporate purposes' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/39020/000118518526003167/feim424b5072826.htm, 2026-07-28). The $17.85m/$0.15 bar itself is from a different source (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-9-10-frequency-electronics-inc-stock/).

finding: Reformation's most recent full quarter before the pre-announced one, Q1 2026, was a GAAP NET LOSS of $12.1m, and its headline 70.3% gross margin was inflated by 904 basis points of a one-time IEEPA tariff refund recovering duties expensed in 2025 - so the entire 'profitable DTC' IPO narrative rests on a non-recurring credit, and the 10 September guide is the first time the company must show a margin without it.
why_not_priced: It is one sentence inside a 'Competitive Strengths' bullet in a 300-page S-1, and the sentence disclosing the $(12.1)m net loss is embedded in a bullet titled 'Adjusted EBITDA'. If the market had focused on it the coverage would not read 'Reformation's IPO filing shows profitable DTC is possible' (Retail Dive, https://www.retaildive.com/news/reformation-ipo-profitable-dtc-model-possible/823857/), the wire summary of the company would not be 'FY2025 net income $12.6m', and 8 of 10 analysts would not have initiated on 2026-08-24 at a $19.25 consensus target, 43% above a $13.50 spot. Ex the 904bp credit the Q1 gross margin was 61.3% against FY2025's 60.2% - i.e. no underlying expansion at all - and no published note or article I could find makes that subtraction.
independence: Revolve Group's Q2 (reported 2026-08-04) separately booked a 162bp gross-margin benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds, https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/revolve-group-announces-second-quarter-2026-financial-results-302842702.html - confirming the refunds are a sector-wide 2026 one-timer being recognised now and not a run-rate, and that Reformation's 904bp version is 5.6x the size of a comparable DTC peer's. NOTE: this finding and finding 3 and finding 4 all rest on the same S-1/424B4 document cluster and should be collapsed to their largest residual.

finding: The IPO over-allotment option was almost entirely unexercised and this was never announced: the two Form 4s filed 2026-09-03 show the underwriters took only 60,298 shares from the Aflalo Family Trust and 149,596 from Refo SCSp (Permira) against a 2,109,375-share option, exactly 5.008% of each holder's base sale, implying the syndicate exercised only ~11% of the greenshoe and covered roughly 1.9m shares - about 5.8 sessions of the 326k-share average daily volume - by buying stock in the open market through August; that stabilising bid ended on 1 September.
why_not_priced: There is no 8-K and no press release announcing the closing of the over-allotment - EDGAR shows exactly one 8-K since listing (2026-08-03, items 5.03/8.01/9.01) and the company's newsroom carries no such release. Recovering the exercise ratio requires pro-rating two separate 09-03 Form 4s against two separate 07-31 Form 4s and against the 2,109,375-share grant in the prospectus. If the market had this, the withdrawal of ~$27m of syndicate demand would have been written up somewhere and the stock's -4.46% five-day slide since 1 September would have a named cause; instead nothing at all was published. The conservative alternative allocation (shoe pro-rated at 15% of each holder's own sale) still gives only a 33% exercise and ~1.4m shares covered, so the finding survives either reading; I size on the conservative end.
independence: Confirmed by a second, independently-filed Form 4 for a different holder showing the identical 5.008% ratio: Aflalo greenshoe 60,298 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1787117/000110465926105131/tm2624653-1_4seq1.xml against base sale 1,204,029 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1787117/000110465926089201/0001104659-26-089201.txt. Also independently, short interest rose 147.4% to 879,261 shares between 30 July and 14 August, https://www.thecerbatgem.com/2026/08/30/short-interest-in-reformation-inc-nyseref-grows-by-147-4.html - real selling pressure was being absorbed by something during the stabilisation window.

finding: The Q2 result itself carries essentially zero surprise capacity: the 424B4 pre-announced net revenue of $154.0-155.0m, gross profit $102.6-103.4m, net income $11.726-11.999m and adjusted EBITDA $24.9-25.3m for the thirteen weeks ended 2026-06-27 - a range one million dollars wide on $154m - so the classic first-post-IPO 'blowout beat' pop is arithmetically unavailable and the entire move is the first-ever Q3/FY guide.
why_not_priced: Newly-listed companies overwhelmingly beat their first print and pop, and that base rate is what a reader with no baseline history reaches for - the sealed baseline here has n=0 reactions and no option chain, so nothing in the price is stating an expected move at all. This name specifically cannot beat, because it told everyone in July what the quarter would be. If that asymmetry were priced you would not see a $19.25 consensus target set on 2026-08-24 sitting 43% above spot; the sell-side is still underwriting a re-rate that only a guide can deliver. Also note the pre-announced range implies +23.1% to +23.9% revenue growth against Q1 2026's +30.4% - a 6.5pt deceleration that the 'twenty consecutive quarters of double-digit growth' wire framing obscures.
independence: none - this rests on the same prospectus document as findings 1 and 4 and should be collapsed into that source cluster; the analyst-target side is corroborated separately at https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/REF/forecast/

finding: Cutting the other way and genuinely material: 9,478,821 of the 14,062,500 IPO shares were PRIMARY, and the company is applying ~$125.1m of net proceeds to repay term loans that stood at $246.7m at 2026-06-27 - so interest expense roughly halves from Q3 onward, which is the single biggest driver of the gap between Q1's $15.9m adjusted EBITDA and its $(12.1)m net loss, and it means the first guided quarter's below-the-line is structurally better than any quarter in the historicals.
why_not_priced: The popular framing of this deal is a Permira cash-out - Refo SCSp still holds 28.9m shares and 49.2% - and the widely-quoted headline number is the $210.9m 'IPO raise', not the $125.1m of debt retirement. Combined with the permanent removal of the IEEPA tariff drag (which cost FY2025 364bp of gross margin), FY2026 adjusted EBITDA can be guided well above FY2025's $45.0m even with the refund stripped out, which is the plausible route to this print going the other way. If this were fully in the price the stock would not be at a 52-week low with a levered-equity discount still visibly applied.
independence: Sector demand is holding up, which is what this needs to work: URBN reported record Q2 sales on 2026-08-26 with Anthropologie retail comps +6%, https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/26/3351678/4732/en/urbn-reports-record-q2-sales-and-profits.html - the closest listed read on the Reformation customer, given after Reformation last spoke on 2026-07-30. finding: Q4 FY25 is a freak comp that Q4 FY26 almost certainly cannot lap: last year's June quarter did $36.0m of gross profit on $227.8m of revenue at a 15.8% gross margin (vs 11.4% the prior year and 12.5% for FY25 as a whole) and $12.2m of adjusted EBITDA, whereas Q3 FY26's gross margin was 12.8% and DOWN 80bp YoY, so AENT needs roughly $281m of June-quarter revenue (+23.5% YoY) just to hold gross profit dollars flat.

A market that had read it would have marked down the index-inclusion optionality that the July information statement had just advertised, and would have asked about a four-week period of operating under an invalid charter.

finding: The true tradeable float is far smaller than any data vendor shows: the DEF 14C states that as of 2026-06-24 only 3,371,581 Class A shares — 3.0% of the 110,979,630 total shares — were held by unrestricted shareholders, against a 20-day average volume of roughly 18,000 shares (~$96k) a day, so the earnings print is effectively the only liquidity window in the quarter for anyone wanting out.

A market that knew the real float were 3.4m shares would not price this at a 14% typical print reaction — it would price it wider, and there is no options market pricing it at all.

finding: The Q2 call on 2026-09-11 is a 'pre-recorded conference call and webcast' — the first pre-recorded RENT earnings call in at least four quarters; the Q2 FY25 (2025-08-25), Q4 FY25 (2026-03-24) and Q1 FY26 (2026-05-19) announcements all said 'conference call and live webcast', so management has removed live analyst Q&A for this print while the company is run by an interim CEO.

If the market had focused on it there would be at least one note or headline framing the format change; instead the only coverage of the 2026-08-21 release is the date itself (StockTitan headline 'Rent the Runway to Report Q2 2026 Results Sept. 11'). The 25-delta skew cannot have absorbed it either — the baseline records no options market on this name at all, so there is no priced directional statement anywhere.
independence: Corroborated by an independent primary document with no overlap: the 2026-09-01 8-K establishing a $10m incremental term loan, i.e. management raised money and then removed the venue where it would be asked why. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1468327/000095010326013373/dp252774_8k.htm

finding: RENT borrowed a $10,000,000 incremental term loan on 2026-09-01 'for working capital and other general corporate purposes' — ten days before the print and after the 2026-07-31 quarter end — even though the 10-Q states the minimum liquidity covenant was PERMANENTLY REMOVED by the First Amendment of 2026-01-28 and the Second Amendment of 2026-04-01 already lets it PIK interest until 2027-05-03; with no covenant to cure and no cash interest to service, the only reason left to take sponsor money is operating cash, which implies a Q2 cash balance far below the $37.1m at 2026-04-30 and the $43.6m at 2025-07-31.
why_not_priced: The 8-K is public and the stock has fallen, so the fact of the loan is partly in; what is not in is the arithmetic, which needs three documents read together. RENT burned $26.8m of cash in Q2 last year ($70.4m at 2025-04-30 to $43.6m at 2025-07-31); even at half that rate on the cut inventory plan, cash at 2026-07-31 lands near $20-27m against $157.1m of long-term debt and a $92m market cap. If the market had done that sum the stock would not need the print to find the number, and there would be a note somewhere stating a Q2 cash estimate — there is none, because the baseline notes this name is not well covered and there is no option chain to express it in.
independence: Partly self-limiting and I am flagging it rather than hiding it: the $6m cash component of the 2026-09-03 settlement (finding 3) was agreed two days after this loan, so roughly $3.1m of the $10m is plausibly earmarked for that and is NOT operating burn — which is exactly why I sized this at -3.0 rather than at what a pure working-capital read would justify. Independent corroboration of the burn trajectory itself, from a different filing: Note 3 of the 2026-06-03 10-Q, cash $37.1m and operating cash flow $(3.8)m versus $8.3m a year earlier. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001468327/000146832726000031/rent-20260430.htm
source_date: 2026-09-01 (Third Amendment to Amended and Restated Credit Agreement, dated 2026-09-01; NOT the Oct 2025 A&R, the Jan 2026 First Amendment or the Apr 2026 Second Amendment)

finding: On 2026-09-03 RENT signed a $9,000,000 Stipulation and Agreement of Settlement of the November 2022 IPO securities class action — $6m cash plus $3m in Class A stock, with insurers paying ~$2.9m and the company ~$3.1m — eight days before the print and five weeks after the 2026-07-31 balance sheet date, so under recognised-subsequent-event treatment the charge lands in the Q2 GAAP numbers being reported on 2026-09-11, and the stock component is ~1.1m new shares (~3.3%) on a 33.59m share count.

The settlement was agreed after the quarter closed and after the earnings date was announced, so it cannot be in consensus by construction. If it were priced there would be a revised GAAP loss estimate in circulation; on a name with essentially one analyst there is not.
independence: Rests on a different document from findings 1, 2 and 4. The absence of a prior accrual is confirmed from a separate filing, the Q1 FY26 10-Q legal proceedings note. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001468327/000146832726000031/rent-20260430.htm

finding: FY26 guidance cuts rental product acquired to $45-50m from $74.9m in FY25 — a ~35% reduction in the inventory that is the product — while ending Active Subscriber growth has already decelerated from ~+20% y/y in Q4 FY25 to +5.8% y/y in Q1 FY26 (155,692), and the dominant live customer complaint is that the assortment is empty ('tiny inventory with items rarely available for rent', 'items marked available now that aren't available in any size').
why_not_priced: The guidance line and the subscriber line are each in the wire; the linkage is not, and the linkage is what sets the Q3 subscriber guide given on 2026-09-11. The Q2 comp is 146,373 actives, which last year fell sequentially from Q1, so a flat sequential quarter still prints ~+6% y/y and the headline metric looks fine — the damage shows up in the forward guide, which is the part no one has modelled. If the market had connected the capex cut to churn there would be a subscriber estimate below the +5.8% trend in circulation; the only public framing is 'revenue up 29%'.
independence: Different-source corroboration of the assortment problem, from customer-facing data rather than filings: https://uk.trustpilot.com/review/www.renttherunway.com . Note the revenue/subscriber divergence itself is visible in the same 2026-06-03 release as the guidance, so this finding rests on one press release plus one consumer source, not two filings.
